susceptible_pests: Aphids (Maahu), Thrips (Chitra)

susceptible_diseases: Damping-off (seedling rot), Early blight (Agati Rog)

susceptible_pests: Aphids (Maahu), Whiteflies (Safed makkhi), Thrips

susceptible_diseases: Early blight (Agati jhulsa), Septoria leaf spot (Septoria ka dhabba)

disease_management: Field care: Ensure good air circulation by spacing plants properly and pruning lower leaves. Avoid overhead watering. Natural control: Spray cow urine solution. Spray if needed: Use copper oxychloride if spots appear on leaves, following the instructions on the packet.

susceptible_diseases: Early blight, Septoria leaf spot, Damping-off (seedling rot)

susceptible_diseases: Early blight, Late blight, Powdery mildew

disease_management: Field care: Ensure good air circulation by spacing plants adequately. Remove and destroy any infected leaves or plants immediately. Natural control: Spray with cow urine solution. susceptible_pests: Whiteflies, Thrips, Fruit borers

susceptible_diseases: Early blight, Late blight, Powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, frequent rains, cool weather, dense plant growth
disease_management: Field care: Ensure good air circulation by pruning lower leaves. Avoid overhead watering. Natural control: Spray cow urine solution. Spray if needed: Use copper oxychloride if blight appears, and spray sulfur if you see powdery mildew.

susceptible_pests: Fruit borer (fruit worm), whiteflies, thrips
pest_risk_factors: Warm weather, continuous tomato cropping, nearby cotton or chilli fields
pest_management: Field care: Pick off and destroy any fruit with holes. Use sticky traps to catch whiteflies and thrips. Natural control: Encourage spiders and ladybugs. Spray if needed: Use neem oil spray every 7-10 days, or ask your local shop for a safe pesticide if the problem is really bad.
susceptible_diseases: Early blight, late blight, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, rain, cool nights, infected seeds or seedlings
disease_management: Field care: Remove and burn any leaves or fruit with spots. Make sure plants have good air flow. Water in the morning so leaves dry quickly. susceptible_pests: Fruit borer (fruit worm), whiteflies, thrips
pest_risk_factors: Warm weather, continuous tomato cropping, nearby cotton or chilli fields
pest_management: Field care: Pick off and destroy any fruit with holes. Set up pheromone traps to catch fruit borer moths. Natural control: Use yellow sticky traps for whiteflies and thrips. susceptible_diseases: Early blight, late blight, fruit rot

susceptible_pests: Fruit borer (fruit worm), whiteflies, thrips

pest_management: Field care: Pick off and destroy any fruit with holes. Use sticky traps to catch whiteflies and thrips. Natural control: Encourage spiders and ladybugs. Spray if needed: Use neem oil spray every week, or ask your local shop for a mild insecticide if the problem is severe.
susceptible_diseases: Early blight, late blight, fruit rot

susceptible_pests: Fruit borer (fruit worm), whiteflies, aphids
pest_risk_factors: Warm weather, nearby fields with pests, not checking plants regularly
pest_management: Field care: Pick off and destroy any fruit worms you see. Keep the field clean of weeds. Natural control: Use yellow sticky traps for whiteflies and aphids. Spray if needed: If pests are many, spray neem oil or ask your local shop for a suitable pesticide.
susceptible_diseases: Early blight, late blight, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: Too much moisture on leaves, humid weather, infected seeds or seedlings

main_stage: Pre-sowing : Involves selecting healthy mother/finger rhizomes and treating them with fungicides like Mancozeb
susceptible_pests: rhizome scale, shoot borer, white grubs
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, planting infested seed rhizomes, and fields with unrotted cow dung manure
pest_management: Field care: Select only clean, spot-free seed rhizomes for planting and clear all weeds from the field. Natural control: Apply neem cake to the soil during final land preparation to keep soil pests away. Spray if needed: If you see scale insects on the seed rhizomes, dip them in a mixture of dimethoate liquid and water before planting.
susceptible_diseases: rhizome rot, seed rot, leaf spot
disease_risk_factors: water pooling in the field, poor drainage, and planting already diseased or damaged seed rhizomes
disease_management: Field care: Make raised beds for planting to let extra water drain out easily and never let water stand in the field. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma with well-rotted cow dung and apply it to the soil before planting. Spray if needed: Treat the seed rhizomes by soaking them in a mancozeb medicine water mix for thirty minutes before sowing to prevent rot.

susceptible_pests: San Jose scale, woolly apple aphid, mite eggs
pest_risk_factors: Unpruned dead wood, loose bark on the trunk, and dry winter weather
pest_management: Field care: Scrape off loose bark from the trunk and main branches to remove hiding pests. Natural control: Paint the lower trunk with a mix of lime and water. Spray if needed: Spray winter spray oil or tree spray oil thoroughly on the entire tree during late dormancy to suffocate pest eggs.
susceptible_diseases: Apple scab, powdery mildew, canker
disease_risk_factors: Fallen infected leaves left on the ground, dead branches, and wet winter snow or rain
disease_management: Field care: Collect and burn all fallen leaves and pruned branches from the orchard floor. Natural control: Apply a thick paste of cow dung and clay on cut ends after pruning. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based blue medicine on the trees after pruning to protect cuts from rot.

main_stage: Pre-sowing : Involves selecting healthy mother/finger rhizomes and treating them with fungicides like Mancozeb
susceptible_pests: shoot borer caterpillar, leaf roller, thrips, scale insects
pest_risk_factors: high humidity, cloudy weather, water pooling in the field, and weeds growing around the plants
pest_management: Field care: Cut and burn the infected shoots showing holes and yellow leaves, and keep the field free of weeds. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soap water on the leaves and stems. Spray if needed: Use a mild insecticide recommended by your local cooperative if you see heavy caterpillar damage.
susceptible_diseases: rhizome rot, leaf spot, leaf blotch
disease_risk_factors: heavy rains, water logging in the soil, clayey soil with poor drainage, and warm humid days
disease_management: Field care: Dig small channels to drain out all standing water from the field immediately. Natural control: Apply friendly fungus powder like Trichoderma mixed with well-rotted cow dung near the plant roots. Spray if needed: Spray a copper-based blue medicine on the leaves and drench the soil around the base to stop rot.

susceptible_pests: San Jose scale, woolly apple aphid, European red mite
pest_risk_factors: Warm winter days, dry bark, and old cracked wood where pests hide
pest_management: Field care: Scrub the tree trunks with a jute gunny bag to remove loose bark and hiding pests. Natural control: Keep ladybugs and lacewings in the orchard as they eat these pests. Spray if needed: Spray a mix of horticultural mineral oil or tree spray oil with clean water thoroughly on the trunk and branches before the green tips open.
susceptible_diseases: Apple scab, powdery mildew, canker
disease_risk_factors: Wet weather, damp soil, and fallen leaves from last year left on the ground
disease_management: Field care: Clean the orchard floor by raking and burying or burning all fallen leaves and pruned twigs. Natural control: Apply a paste of cow dung and clay on cut ends of branches to block infections. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based blue medicine liquid on the branches to protect the new buds from rotting.

susceptible_pests: apple aphid, San Jose scale, thrips, mites
pest_risk_factors: warm and dry weather, cloudy days, crowded branches that block sunlight
pest_management: Field care: Remove weeds around the tree trunk and prune crowded water sprouts. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky cards near the flowers to catch flying pests and protect ladybugs that eat aphids. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water thoroughly on the buds before they open fully.
susceptible_diseases: apple scab, powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: wet weather, continuous spring rains, morning dew, fallen leaves left on the ground from last year
disease_management: Field care: Clean up and burn all fallen leaves and rotten fruits from the orchard floor. Natural control: Spray a mixture of baking soda and water to stop early fungus growth. Spray if needed: Apply a basic copper spray or a standard anti-scab medicine just as the pink buds begin to show.

susceptible_pests: apple aphid, thrips, spider mites, blossom thrips
pest_risk_factors: warm and dry weather, lack of moisture in the soil, weeds growing under the trees
pest_management: Field care: Keep the orchard floor clean by removing weeds and wild grass. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky traps on branches to catch flying pests, and protect ladybugs which eat aphids. Spray if needed: Spray a mild neem oil mixture on the leaves and branches after the flowers have fallen.
susceptible_diseases: apple scab, powdery mildew, blossom blight
disease_risk_factors: cloudy days, frequent spring rains, wet leaves, and dense branches that block sunlight
disease_management: Field care: Prune crowded branches to let sunlight and fresh air pass through the tree. Natural control: Spray a mixture of baking soda and water on the leaves to stop white powdery spots. Spray if needed: Apply a basic copper spray or a simple fungicide recommended by your local cooperative right after the petals fall.

susceptible_pests: San Jose scale, apple aphid, red spider mite, codling moth worm
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, dusty leaves near farm roads, and crowded branches that block sunlight
pest_management: Field care: Keep the tree basins clean and remove any weeds. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe insect spray recommended by your local cooperative if the pest attack is heavy.
susceptible_diseases: Apple scab, powdery mildew, premature leaf fall
disease_risk_factors: Cloudy days, continuous light rains, high humidity, and wet leaves that do not dry quickly
disease_management: Field care: Prune extra leaves to let sunlight and air pass through the branches easily. Natural control: Spray cow urine mixed with water or use bio-fungicides like Trichoderma on the soil. Spray if needed: Apply a basic copper-based spray or a standard scab control medicine during a clear, dry window of the day.

susceptible_pests: cutworms, termites, wireworms
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, unrotted cow dung manure in the field, residues from the previous crop
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and remove old crop roots. Natural control: Apply neem cake to the soil during land preparation to keep termites away. Spray if needed: Mix neem oil in water and spray on the soil around the young sprouts if you see cut plants.
susceptible_diseases: seedling rot, damping-off, wilt

Natural control: Treat the seeds with Trichoderma powder before sowing to protect the roots. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine on the soil if the young plants start rotting and falling over.

susceptible_pests: Mustard sawfly, Painted bug
pest_risk_factors: Dry soil, warm sunny days, and weeds left growing around the young plants.
pest_management: Field care: Handpick and destroy the black sawfly larvae from the leaves in the early morning. Remove weeds and thin out crowded seedlings to keep the field clean. Natural control: Spray neem water mixed with a little liquid soap on the young leaves. Spray if needed: If you see too many holes in the leaves, use a mild pest-control spray from your local cooperative store.
susceptible_diseases: Damping-off (seedling rot), Downy mildew
disease_risk_factors: Waterlogging in the field, cloudy weather, and sowing seeds too close together.
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any excess water from the field and keep the soil moist but not soggy. Thin out the crowded plants so that sunlight can reach the soil. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder in the soil near the roots. Spray if needed: If seedlings start rotting at the base, spray a simple copper-based medicine to protect them.

susceptible_pests: Mahu or Lahi (Aphids), Katra (Sawfly caterpillar), Painted Bug
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy and cold weather, too much moisture in the air, and sowing plants too close to each other
pest_management: Field care: Pull out extra crowded plants to let sunlight in and remove all weeds. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky cards in the field to catch flying pests and spray neem water on the crop. Spray if needed: If you see too many pests on the stems, spray a mild pest medicine from your local cooperative store.

disease_management: Field care: Drain out any standing water from the field and pluck off the infected lower leaves. Natural control: Spray a mixture of cow urine and water on the plants to build strength. Spray if needed: If white powder or dark spots spread on leaves, spray a copper-based fungus medicine immediately.

susceptible_diseases: Seedling rot, Damping-off (falling of young plants)
disease_risk_factors: Too much water in the soil, cloudy weather, and sowing seeds too deep.

susceptible_pests: Mahu (Aphids), Painted Bug

Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma into the soil before sowing or drench the root zone with it. Spray if needed: If rotting continues, spray a copper-based medicine lightly on the soil and seedlings to stop the spread.

susceptible_pests: Aphids (Mahu or Lahi), Painted Bug

Spray if needed: If the attack is very heavy, spray a mild insect-killing medicine from your local cooperative store during the late afternoon to protect honeybees.
susceptible_diseases: White Rust (Safed Rog), Downy Mildew, Black Spot (Alternaria Blight)
disease_risk_factors: Heavy morning dew, cloudy days, wet soil, and plants growing too close to each other

Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk or cow urine with water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Spray blue copper medicine mixed in water to stop the spots from spreading to the flowers.

susceptible_pests: Aphids (Mahu or Lahi), Painted bug, Cabbage butterfly caterpillars

pest_management: Field care: Walk through the field daily and pluck off the heavily infested pod branches where pests are clustered. susceptible_diseases: Black spot on pods (Alternaria blight), White rust (white powdery spots on leaves and stems)

Spray if needed: If dark spots appear on the pods, spray a standard disease-fighting powder mixed in water to save your seeds from rotting. susceptible_pests: Painted bug (Chitrada keeda), Aphids (Mahu)

pest_management: Field care: Harvest the crop immediately when most pods turn golden yellow to prevent seed loss and bug attacks. Do not leave harvested heaps lying in the field for a long time. susceptible_diseases: Black spot (Alternaria), White rust (Safed ruli)
disease_risk_factors: Sudden late rains, cloudy weather, and high moisture in the soil or air
disease_management: Field care: Cut the crop on a clear sunny day and dry the bundles well on a clean, dry floor. Avoid piling wet plants together to prevent mold. Natural control: Collect and burn the leftover dry plant waste after threshing to clean the soil. Spray if needed: Do not spray any liquid medicines now as the crop is fully ready for cutting.

susceptible_pests: diamondback moth caterpillar, aphids, flea beetles

pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy any visible caterpillars and remove weeds around the field. disease_management: Field care: Keep the field well-drained so water does not stand near the young stems. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma into the soil around the roots during transplanting. Spray if needed: If you see rotting at the base, spray a basic copper-based medicine on the soil and lower leaves.

susceptible_pests: diamondback moth caterpillar, cabbage butterfly worm, aphids, head borer

susceptible_diseases: black rot, downy mildew, damping-off

Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water or use bio-powders like Trichoderma in the soil. Spray if needed: Use a basic copper-based blue medicine spray if black spots or yellow patches spread rapidly.

susceptible_pests: diamondback moth caterpillar, cabbage butterfly caterpillar, aphids

Spray if needed: If the attack is severe, spray a safe caterpillar-killing medicine recommended by your local cooperative during the evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: black rot, clubroot, downy mildew
disease_risk_factors: too much water in the soil, high humidity, water pooling around the plant roots, warm and wet weather

Spray if needed: Spray a copper-based blue medicine mixed in water on the leaves and near the roots if you see dark spots or rotting.

susceptible_pests: diamondback moth caterpillar, cabbage looper, aphids, head borer

pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy any caterpillars and damaged leaves daily. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water on the heads. Spray if needed: Use a mild, farmer-recommended caterpillar spray only on the affected heads during late afternoon.

disease_management: Field care: Keep the soil around the cabbage heads dry and remove any yellowing lower leaves to let air pass. pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and remove old crop roots. Natural control: Use bird perches to let birds eat the worms, or apply neem cake to the soil. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the soil and young sprouts if you see cutworms.
susceptible_diseases: Seed rot, Collar rot, Damping-off
disease_risk_factors: Waterlogging, heavy rain right after sowing, and sowing seeds too deep.
disease_management: Field care: Make sure excess rainwater drains out of the field quickly and do not sow seeds too deep. Natural control: Treat seeds with Trichoderma powder before sowing. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine on the soil near the sprouts if they start rotting.

sub_stage_name: Fruit Ripening and Color Turning to Red
susceptible_pests: Thrips (Churda Murda), Red spider mites, Fruit borer caterpillar
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, cloudy days, and weeds growing around the field boundaries
pest_management: Field care: Collect and bury all bored or damaged chilies away from the field. Natural control: Hang yellow and blue sticky cards near the plants and spray neem water regularly. Spray if needed: Use a mild pest medicine from your local cooperative shop if you see too many caterpillars.
susceptible_diseases: Fruit rot (Koyla rog), Powdery mildew (white ash on leaves)
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, heavy morning dew, cloudy skies, and water standing in the soil
disease_management: Field care: Pluck and destroy any rotting or spotted red chilies immediately to save the healthy ones. Natural control: Spray ten-day-old sour buttermilk mixed with water on the crop. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based blue medicine to stop the rot from spreading further.

sub_stage_name: Final Harvesting and Sun Drying of Pods
susceptible_pests: Fruit borer, thrips, mites, termites
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, keeping harvested chilies directly on the bare soil, and leaving overripe pods on the plant for too long
pest_management: Field care: Harvest the ripe red pods regularly and do not leave them on the plant for too long. Natural control: Dry the harvested chilies on clean plastic sheets or raised platforms to keep termites away. Spray if needed: If you see borers on the remaining crop, spray neem water on the plants.
susceptible_diseases: Fruit rot, pod rot, white powdery mold
disease_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, sudden rains during drying, and piling up wet chilies in thick heaps
disease_management: Field care: Separate and throw away all damaged or spotted chilies before drying the good ones. Natural control: Spread the healthy chilies in a thin, single layer on clean mats under direct sunlight to dry them quickly. Spray if needed: If fruit rot is spreading on the plants, spray a simple copper medicine on a clear sunny day.

susceptible_pests: Aphids (Lahi), Armyworm caterpillars
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, warm days, too much urea fertilizer, and weeds in and around the field
pest_management: Field care: Pull out weeds regularly and do not apply excess urea at this stage. Natural control: Spray homemade neem water or a garlic-chilli mixture. Spray if needed: If the pest attack is severe, use a simple pest-control spray from your local cooperative store.
susceptible_diseases: Leaf rust (Rattua), Powdery mildew (Safed fafundi)
disease_risk_factors: Heavy morning dew, cloudy skies, wet soil, and plants growing too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any standing water and remove infected leaves from the field. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the crop. Spray if needed: Use a basic copper spray or a simple disease medicine from the local store to stop the spread.

susceptible_pests: Girdle beetle, Tobacco caterpillar, Green semilooper, Stem fly
pest_risk_factors: Overcast cloudy weather, high humidity, weeds left growing in the field, and warm days.
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field completely free of weeds as they harbor pests. Put up T-shaped wooden bird perches to attract birds that eat caterpillars. Natural control: Spray neem water or neem oil mixed with a little washing soap. Spray if needed: If you see many cut leaves, spray a mild insect-control medicine from your local government depot.
susceptible_diseases: Yellow mosaic disease, Root rot, Collar rot
disease_risk_factors: Water standing in the field, very dense sowing, and high numbers of whiteflies that spread the yellowing disease.
disease_management: Field care: Make channels to drain out standing rainwater quickly. Pull out any yellowing plants and bury them deep in the soil away from the field. Natural control: Apply friendly bio-fungus powder mixed with well-rotted cow dung near the plant roots. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based disease medicine to protect the new leaves from rotting.

susceptible_pests: leaf webber, capsule borer, gall fly, hawk moth caterpillar

pest_management: Field care: Walk through the field daily, hand-pick any rolled leaves or caterpillars, and destroy them. susceptible_diseases: root rot, stem rot, leaf spot, powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: water standing in the field, heavy rains, high soil moisture, and crowded plants

Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma into the soil or spray it on the plants. Spray if needed: If leaves show dark spots or stems turn black, spray a basic copper-based medicine or sulphur powder mixed in water to stop the spread.

susceptible_pests: Pod borer, Tobacco caterpillar, Semilooper

pest_management: Field care: Walk through your field daily and hand-pick any visible caterpillars or damaged pods. Spray if needed: If you see more than two caterpillars per meter, spray a mild insect medicine recommended by your local cooperative.
susceptible_diseases: Pod blight, Rust, Yellow Mosaic disease

disease_management: Field care: Make sure rainwater drains out of the field quickly and does not stand near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine or sulfur powder mixed in water to protect the developing pods.

susceptible_pests: Tobacco caterpillar, Girdle beetle, Semilooper, Whitefly

Spray if needed: Spray homemade neem seed juice or neem oil mixed with soap water to keep the pests away.
susceptible_diseases: Yellow mosaic disease, Soybean rust, Root rot
disease_risk_factors: Continuous rainy days, water standing in the field, and whiteflies spreading the yellow virus from plant to plant
disease_management: Field care: Pull out any yellow-colored plants immediately and bury them outside the field to stop the disease from spreading. Spray if needed: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water, or use a basic copper medicine from your local store if you see orange rust spots on the leaves.

susceptible_pests: Aphids (Lahi), Armyworms (Katra sundi), Termites (Deemak)
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, dry soil, and putting too much urea fertilizer in the field
pest_management: Field care: Remove weeds regularly and do not put too much urea at one time. Natural control: Spray neem water mixed with a little liquid soap on the leaves. Spray if needed: If the pest attack is very high, ask your local cooperative for a mild pest-killing spray.

disease_risk_factors: Water standing in the field, cloudy days, and plants growing too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Make sure water does not stand in the field and pull out sick plants. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water on the crop. Spray if needed: If you see orange or white spots spreading, spray a basic copper medicine mixed in water.

susceptible_diseases: Root rot, blister blight, collar rot

Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungus powder like Trichoderma into the soil around the roots to fight bad rot. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based blue medicine on the leaves if you see spots or white powdery growth.

susceptible_pests: Red spider mites, tea thrips, tea mosquitoes, termites

pest_management: Field care: Keep the soil covered with dry leaves or straw mulch to save moisture and plant temporary shade bushes like crotalaria. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Use mild pest sprays recommended by your local tea garden guide during early morning or evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: Blister blight, black rot, root rot

disease_management: Field care: Clear out weeds and trim low-hanging branches to let air and sunlight pass through the young plants. Natural control: Apply friendly bio-fungus powder mixed with compost to the soil around the roots. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based medicine on the leaves if you see yellow or dark spots.

susceptible_pests: Red spider mites, Tea thrips, Tea mosquito bug, Green fly
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, lack of shade trees, waterlogging in the root zone, and overgrown weeds around young plants
pest_management: Field care: Keep the tea patch free of weeds and maintain light shade using temporary shade plants. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the underside of the leaves where pests hide. Spray if needed: Use mild pest-control sprays recommended by your local cooperative during early morning or late evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: Blister blight, Black rot, Root rot
disease_risk_factors: Continuous cloudy days, heavy mist, water pooling around the roots, and lack of air flow due to crowded branches
disease_management: Field care: Prune the young bushes properly to let sunlight and air pass through, and clear any blocked water drains. Natural control: Apply organic compost mixed with friendly bio-fungus powder to the soil around the base. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based medicine on the leaves immediately after pruning to protect the open cuts from infection.

susceptible_pests: pod borer, aphids
pest_risk_factors: warm sunny days, dry weather, late harvesting
pest_management: Field care: Harvest the crop as soon as pods turn brown to avoid pest attack. Natural control: Place T-shaped wooden bird perches in the field to attract birds that eat caterpillars. Spray if needed: Spray neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water if you see too many pests.
susceptible_diseases: pod rot, rust
disease_risk_factors: sudden unseasonal rain, high moisture in the soil, dense crop canopy
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any standing water immediately and keep the field dry. Natural control: Remove and burn infected plants away from the field. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine or biological powder like Trichoderma mixed in water if wet weather persists.

susceptible_pests: Tea mosquito bug, Red spider mite, Thrips, Green fly
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather with high humidity, waterlogging in the field, and very hot, dry days
pest_management: Field care: Keep the tea bushes clean and pluck leaves regularly to disturb the pests. Clear all weeds around the bushes. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the underside of the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe pest-control spray recommended by your local cooperative during early morning or late evening.
susceptible_diseases: Blister blight, Black rot, Red rust
disease_risk_factors: Continuous rain, heavy mist, wet leaves for long hours, and too much shade from trees
disease_management: Field care: Cut away extra branches of shade trees to let sunlight reach the tea bushes. Keep the drains clean so water does not stand. Natural control: Spray a mixture of copper powder and water on the affected leaves. Spray if needed: Use a basic disease-control spray on the new buds and leaves right after plucking.

sub_stage_name: Peak Plucking and Maintenance Pruning Cycles
susceptible_pests: Tea Mosquito Bug, Red Spider Mite, Thrips, Green Fly
pest_risk_factors: Overcast weather with high humidity brings the mosquito bug, while hot and dry sunny weeks bring heavy mite attacks.
pest_management: Field care: Pluck leaves regularly every week to remove pest eggs and keep the bushes well-trimmed to let sunlight in. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water thoroughly on the underside of the leaves where pests hide. Spray if needed: Use mild, recommended pest sprays only after a round of plucking and wait for at least ten days before the next harvest.
susceptible_diseases: Blister Blight, Black Rot, Red Rust
disease_risk_factors: Continuous misty days, heavy morning dew, water logging in the soil, and too much shade from overhead trees.
disease_management: Field care: Trim the shade trees to let sunlight reach the tea bushes and clear out blocked drains to stop water from standing. Natural control: Spray liquid copper-based mixtures or organic bio-fungicides on the affected patches. Spray if needed: Apply a light copper spray immediately after pruning to protect the cut stems from rotting.

susceptible_pests: thrips, aphids, jassids, whiteflies
pest_risk_factors: hot and dry weather, lack of rain, weeds around the field boundaries
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field and borders free of weeds to stop pests from hiding. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the young leaves. Spray if needed: If you see heavy leaf curling, spray a mild, recommended pest medicine from your local cooperative store.
susceptible_diseases: root rot, seedling blight, damping-off
disease_risk_factors: waterlogging in the field, heavy clay soil, cloudy weather with too much moisture
disease_management: Field care: Make small channels to drain out any standing rainwater immediately. Natural control: Apply friendly fungus powder like Trichoderma mixed with well-rotted cow dung near the plant base. Spray if needed: If young plants start rotting and falling over, drench the soil around them with a basic copper-based medicine.

susceptible_pests: green jassids, whiteflies, thrips, aphids
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, dry spells, and too much urea fertilizer
pest_management: Field care: Remove all weeds around the cotton plants and set up yellow sticky traps to catch flying insects. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water to repel young pests. Spray if needed: If leaves start curling downwards, spray a mild, recommended insecticide from your local cooperative store.
susceptible_diseases: root rot, leaf spot, damping off
disease_risk_factors: water pooling in the field, heavy clay soil, and continuous rain
disease_management: Field care: Make small channels to drain out any standing water from the root zone immediately. Natural control: Apply Trichoderma bio-fungicide mixed with well-rotted cow dung near the base of the plants. Spray if needed: If you see dark spots on leaves or rotting stems, spray a copper-based medicine mixed in clean water.

susceptible_pests: green jassids, whiteflies, thrips, spotted bollworm
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, too much nitrogen fertilizer, and dry spells
pest_management: Field care: Remove weeds around the field and install yellow sticky traps to catch flying pests. susceptible_diseases: root rot, leaf spot, grey mildew

Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma in compost and apply near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine on the leaves if dark spots start to spread.

susceptible_pests: ants, cutworms, whiteflies
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, ants carrying away seeds, hot and dry weather
pest_management: Field care: Keep the nursery bed moist but not wet to stop ants. Natural control: Sprinkle turmeric powder or wood ash around the nursery borders to keep ants away. Spray if needed: Spray mild neem water on the soil if you see tiny crawling insects.
susceptible_diseases: damping-off, seed rot
disease_risk_factors: too much water, crowded sowing, heavy clay soil, cloudy weather
disease_management: Field care: Sow seeds thinly on raised beds so water drains out quickly. Natural control: Mix friendly fungus powder like Trichoderma into the soil before sowing. Spray if needed: Spray copper medicine mixed in water on the soil if young seedlings start falling over.

susceptible_pests: American bollworm, pink bollworm, whitefly, aphids, jassids

pest_management: Field care: Hang yellow sticky traps for sucking pests and install light traps to catch adult moths. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil to stop young pests from feeding. Spray if needed: Use a mild, farmer-recommended insect medicine only if you see more than two bollworms per plant.
susceptible_diseases: Root rot, leaf spot, black arm disease
disease_risk_factors: Water standing in the field, heavy rains followed by sudden hot sun, and crowded plants
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any excess water from the field immediately and remove infected plants. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma in well-rotted cow dung and apply near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine on the leaves if dark spots start spreading rapidly.

susceptible_pests: Pink bollworm, whitefly, cotton stainer bug
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, late-season warmth, and leaving cracked bolls open on the plant for too long
pest_management: Field care: Pick the burst cotton bolls early and regularly to prevent worms from entering. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky cards to trap whiteflies and use pheromone traps to catch pink bollworm moths. Spray if needed: Use a neem seed kernel extract spray or a mild, farmer-recommended pest spray only on highly affected plants.
susceptible_diseases: Boll rot, grey mildew, sooty mould
disease_risk_factors: Unseasonal rains, heavy morning dew, wet soil, and shade from overcrowded plants
disease_management: Field care: Remove damaged or rotted bolls immediately and keep the field free of weeds to let sunlight in. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water to keep mildews away. Spray if needed: Apply a simple copper-based blue medicine spray if the bolls start rotting due to sudden rains.

susceptible_pests: pink bollworm, cotton stainer bug, whitefly
pest_risk_factors: leaving picked cotton in the open, delayed harvesting, warm and humid days, keeping the crop in the field for too long
pest_management: Field care: Pick cotton as soon as bolls open and do not let them sit on the plant. Pull out and destroy the crop stalks immediately after the final picking to stop pests from breeding. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky traps to catch whiteflies and use pheromone traps to monitor pink bollworm. Spray if needed: Use a neem seed kernel extract spray if you see small pink worms inside the remaining bolls.
susceptible_diseases: boll rot, sooty mould
disease_risk_factors: unseasonal winter rains, high humidity, dew on open bolls, pest damage on bolls that lets water inside
disease_management: Field care: Pick the clean cotton early in the morning after the dew dries up and keep infected bolls separate. Clean the field of all fallen leaves and rotten bolls after harvesting. Natural control: Dry the harvested cotton thoroughly under the sun before storing it in a dry room. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine on the plants if unseasonal rains occur during the final picking stage.

susceptible_pests: crickets, hairy caterpillars, cutworms
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, weeds around the field borders, and warm sunny days
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field borders clean and remove all weeds where pests hide. Natural control: Place bamboo perches in the field to invite birds that eat these insects. Spray if needed: Spray neem water on the young seedlings during the evening.
susceptible_diseases: seedling rot, damping-off
disease_risk_factors: waterlogging in the field, clayey soil, and cloudy weather with high moisture
disease_management: Field care: Make small channels to drain out any standing water immediately. Natural control: Mix rotten cow dung with friendly bio-fungicide powder and apply to the soil. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based medicine mixed in water on the soil if seedlings start rotting.

susceptible_pests: jute hairy caterpillar, yellow mite, semilooper, indigo caterpillar

pest_management: Field care: Handpick and destroy caterpillar egg masses and young leaf-eating larvae. Use a hand hoe for weeding to disturb soil-dwelling pests. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: Use safe, common pest-control sprays from the local cooperative store only if the leaf damage increases.
susceptible_diseases: damping-off, seedling blight, root rot
disease_risk_factors: waterlogged fields, clayey soils, cloudy weather, and sowing seeds too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Thin out weak seedlings to let air and sunlight pass through, and clear any standing water from the field. Natural control: Mix well-rotted cow dung with friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma and apply it to the soil. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine on the soil and young plants if you see seedlings rotting at the base.

susceptible_pests: jute semilooper, hairy caterpillar, yellow mite, bihar hairy caterpillar

pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy visible caterpillars and their egg masses from the leaves. Install bamboo perches in the field to invite insect-eating birds. susceptible_pests: jute semilooper, hairy caterpillar, yellow mite, bihar hairy caterpillar

pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy caterpillars and their eggs from the leaves. Use bamboo perches in the field to invite birds that eat these pests. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe insect spray recommended by your local cooperative only on affected patches.
susceptible_diseases: stem rot, root rot, leaf spot

susceptible_pests: jute semilooper, hairy caterpillar, yellow mite

pest_management: Field care: Keep the basin around the young sapling clean and free of weeds. Remove any dead wood or dry twigs from the field. susceptible_pests: bark eating caterpillar, shoot borer, aphids

pest_management: Field care: Keep the tree trunk clean and remove any wooden webs or tunnels made of sawdust on the bark. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the branches and trunk to keep small insects away.

susceptible_pests: shoot and fruit borer, whitefly, jassids, red spider mites

susceptible_diseases: damping off, leaf spot, collar rot

susceptible_diseases: damping off, leaf spot, collar rot

susceptible_diseases: fruit rot, phomopsis blight, powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: high humidity, water pooling around the plant base, and dense leaves that block sunlight and air

susceptible_pests: eggplant fruit and shoot borer, spider mites, whiteflies

susceptible_pests: Thrips, onion maggots
pest_risk_factors: Dry weather, hot days, and cracked soil that lets pests reach the bulbs
pest_management: Field care: Stop watering the crop completely two weeks before harvesting to let the soil dry. Natural control: Keep the field free of weeds where pests hide. Spray if needed: If you see tiny yellow or black insects on the leaves, spray neem oil mixed with soapy water.
susceptible_diseases: Purple blotch, bulb rot, neck rot
disease_risk_factors: Too much water in the soil, cloudy weather, and harvesting during rains
disease_management: Field care: Ensure all water drains out of the field and do not damage the bulbs during digging. Natural control: Dry the harvested garlic bulbs in shade with good air flow for at least three days. Spray if needed: If you see purple spots on leaves or rotting at the neck, spray a basic copper-based medicine on the crop before harvesting.

susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, cutworms, ants
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, warm sunny days, weeds around the young sprouts, and old crop waste left in the field
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and remove all weeds around the new sprouts. Hand-pick the orange-red beetles in the cool morning hours. Natural control: Sprinkle wood ash on the young leaves to keep beetles away, or spray neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: If the damage is heavy, spray a mild, basic insect medicine recommended by your local cooperative shop on the soil around the stems.
susceptible_diseases: seedling rot, damping-off, collar rot
disease_risk_factors: too much watering, water standing in the beds, cloudy weather, and sowing seeds too deep in heavy clay soil
disease_management: Field care: Avoid overwatering and ensure extra water drains out of the beds quickly. Keep the soil loose but do not disturb the roots. Natural control: Treat the soil with friendly bio-fungus powder like Trichoderma before sowing or mix it into the wet soil. Spray if needed: If young seedlings start falling over and rotting at the base, drench the soil around them with a basic copper-based blue medicine mixed in water.

susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, aphids, thrips, leaf miner
pest_risk_factors: warm and sunny days, dry soil, weeds around the young plants, and lack of moisture
pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy the orange-red beetles from the young leaves in the early morning when they are slow. Keep the field free of weeds. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with mild soap water on the leaves, or dust fine wood ash on the young seedlings early in the morning. Spray if needed: If the damage is severe, spray a mild, recommended insect-killing medicine from the local store on a clear afternoon.
susceptible_diseases: damping-off, collar rot, downy mildew
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, water pooling near the roots, clayey soil that stays wet, and sowing seeds too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Avoid overwatering and ensure extra water drains out of the field quickly. Gently loosen the soil around the base to help it dry. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma in well-rotted cow dung and apply it near the roots. Spray if needed: If the baby plants start rotting at the base, spray a copper-based blue medicine on the soil and leaves to stop the spread.

susceptible_pests: Aphids, Thrips, Red Pumpkin Beetle, Leaf Miner
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, cloudy days, weeds around the field, and too much nitrogen fertilizer.
pest_management: Field care: Remove all weeds regularly and keep the field clean. Natural control: Use yellow and blue sticky traps to catch flying pests, and spray neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: If the attack is severe, spray a mild insecticide recommended by your local cooperative during the evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: Powdery Mildew, Downy Mildew, Fusarium Wilt
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, cloudy weather, water logging around the roots, and planting vines too close to each other.
disease_management: Field care: Avoid watering the leaves directly, channel water only to the roots, and remove any yellowing or spotted leaves immediately. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water or use Trichoderma bio-fungicide in the soil. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based fungicide on a clear, sunny morning if spots appear on the leaves.

susceptible_pests: fruit fly, aphids, thrips, red pumpkin beetle
pest_risk_factors: hot and dry weather, yellow flowers attracting insects, weeds around the field, water stress
pest_management: Field care: Hang yellow sticky traps to catch small sucking insects and use poison bait traps for fruit flies. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild insect spray from the local store only in the evening so you do not harm the friendly honeybees that pollinate your flowers.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, water touching the leaves, over-watering the soil
disease_management: Field care: Keep the watermelons off the wet soil by placing dry straw under them and water only at the root level. Natural control: Spray a mix of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves to stop white powdery spots. Spray if needed: Use a basic copper or sulfur powder spray if you see dark spots spreading on the leaves.

susceptible_pests: fruit fly, red pumpkin beetle, aphids, thrips
pest_risk_factors: hot and dry weather, water dripping on leaves, weeds around the field, and leaving damaged fruits on the ground
pest_management: Field care: Hang yellow and blue sticky traps near the plants, and use poison bait traps specifically for fruit flies. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with mild soap water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild chemical spray recommended by your local cooperative during early morning hours if the pest attack is very high.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, water pooling around the fruits, and touching plants when they are wet
disease_management: Field care: Place dry grass or plastic sheets under the growing watermelons to keep them off the wet soil. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves to stop white powdery spots. Spray if needed: Apply a basic copper-based medicine on the soil and leaves if you see dark spots spreading.

susceptible_pests: Fruit fly, red spider mites, aphids
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, over-ripe fruits left on the ground, and weeds around the field
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and harvest ripe melons on time to prevent attracting flies. Natural control: Hang simple yellow sticky traps and plastic bottle fruit fly traps with sweet bait around the patch. Spray if needed: Use a mild neem oil spray on the leaves if you see tiny crawling pests.
susceptible_diseases: Fruit rot, powdery mildew, downy mildew
disease_risk_factors: Water touching the fruits, cloudy weather, wet soil, and watering late in the evening
disease_management: Field care: Place dry grass or small wooden blocks under the melons so they do not touch wet soil. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water on the leaves to stop white powdery spots. Spray if needed: Use a basic copper-based spray only if you see dark rotting spots on the fruits.

susceptible_pests: ants, cutworms, aphids
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, unrotted cow dung manure in the field, warm sunny days
pest_management: Field care: Keep the soil moist but not wet to stop ants from carrying away seeds. Use well-rotted manure to avoid cutworms. Natural control: Sprinkle wood ash around the sowing lines to keep crawling insects away. Spray if needed: Spray neem water on the soil surface if you see tiny insects crawling near the emerging sprouts.
susceptible_diseases: seedling rot, damping-off
disease_risk_factors: waterlogging in the beds, sowing seeds too deep, cloudy weather with high humidity
disease_management: Field care: Make proper channels to drain out extra water from the beds and do not overwater. Natural control: Treat the seeds with friendly Trichoderma powder before sowing to protect them in the soil. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based blue medicine mixed in water on the soil if the young seedlings start falling over and rotting.

susceptible_pests: Aphids, leaf eating caterpillars
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, and weeds growing around the young plants
pest_management: Field care: Pull out all weeds regularly to keep the field clean. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe insect spray from the local store if you see too many pests.
susceptible_diseases: Damping-off, root rot
disease_risk_factors: Too much water in the soil, poor drainage, and sowing seeds too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Do not let water stand in the field and keep the soil moist but not wet. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma in the soil near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper medicine on the soil and young plants if they start rotting.

susceptible_pests: Aphids (green flies), thrips, leaf-eating caterpillars
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, warm days, and weeds growing around the coriander plants
pest_management: Field care: Pull out all weeds regularly to keep the field clean and let in sunlight. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with a little soap water. Spray if needed: If the pest attack is very high, spray a mild, safe insect-killing medicine bought from the local store during the evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: Powdery mildew (white ash-like powder on leaves), stem gall (swellings on stems), root rot
disease_risk_factors: Cool nights with heavy morning dew, cloudy days, over-watering, and plants growing too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Avoid watering the field in the late evening and keep the soil moist but not muddy. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water, or use Trichoderma bio-powder mixed in compost near the roots. Spray if needed: If you see white powder on the leaves, spray a soluble sulphur powder mixed in water immediately to save the crop.

susceptible_pests: aphids, green caterpillars, thrips
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, cool nights, and too much nitrogen fertilizer
pest_management: Field care: Remove weeds regularly and do not over-water the crop. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with liquid soap, or use yellow sticky traps to catch flying pests. Spray if needed: Use a mild, farmer-recommended pest spray only in the late afternoon to protect visiting honeybees.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, stem gall, wilt
disease_risk_factors: cool mornings with heavy dew, cloudy days, and water standing in the field
disease_management: Field care: Keep the field free of stagnant water and remove any infected plants immediately. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water or use bio-powders like Trichoderma in the soil. Spray if needed: Spray a basic sulfur powder mix on the leaves at the first sign of white ash-like spots.

sub_stage_name: Seed Setting and Green Seed Stage
susceptible_pests: Aphids (Lahi), Thrips, Seed Chalcid Wasp
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, and warm day temperatures during the seed formation stage.
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field free of weeds and monitor the green seed clusters daily. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water early in the morning. Spray if needed: If the pest attack is severe, spray a mild, recommended insecticide from your local cooperative store during the late afternoon to protect visiting honeybees.
susceptible_diseases: Powdery Mildew (Chhachhiya), Stem Gall (Tumor disease), Grain Mold
disease_risk_factors: Cool nights with warm days, heavy morning dew, and too much moisture in the soil.
disease_management: Field care: Avoid watering the crop late in the evening and ensure good sunlight reaches the plants. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water on the crop. Spray if needed: Spray a soluble sulfur powder mixed in water as soon as you see the white powdery spots on the leaves or stems.

susceptible_pests: cutworms, white grubs, termites
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, unrotted cow dung manure in the field, fields with previous crop residues
pest_management: Field care: Flood the field lightly to force pests to the surface so birds can eat them, and manually collect and destroy grubs. Natural control: Mix neem cake powder into the soil around the ridges. Spray if needed: Apply neem oil mixed with soap water on the soil surface near the sprouts in the evening.
susceptible_diseases: seed piece decay, damping off, black scurf
disease_risk_factors: excessive soil moisture, poorly drained heavy clay soils, planting damaged or unhealed cut seed potatoes
disease_management: Field care: Avoid overwatering and ensure water drains out of the field quickly. Natural control: Treat the soil with friendly Trichoderma bio-fungicide powder mixed with well-rotted compost before planting. Spray if needed: Spray the soil ridges with a simple copper-based blue medicine powder mixed in water if sprouts start rotting at the base.

susceptible_pests: Aphids, Jassids, Whiteflies, Cutworms
pest_risk_factors: Warm days with cloudy weather, dry soil conditions, and weeds growing around the potato plants.
pest_management: Field care: Remove all weeds regularly and keep the soil loose around the plants. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves, and use yellow sticky cards to catch flying pests. Spray if needed: Use a mild pest medicine from the local store if you see too many insects sucking the leaf juice.
susceptible_diseases: Early Blight, Black Scurf, Damping Off
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, cloudy days, wet soil, and planting potato seeds too close to each other.
disease_management: Field care: Avoid watering the field too much and ensure extra water drains out quickly. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma into the soil around the plants. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine on the leaves if dark spots start to appear.

susceptible_pests: Aphids, Whiteflies, Potato Tuber Moth
pest_risk_factors: Warm and dry weather, cracked soil that exposes growing potatoes, and weeds around the field
pest_management: Field care: Keep the soil well-covered around the plant base to hide growing potatoes from moths. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild pest medicine from the local store if you see too many insects sucking the leaf juice.
susceptible_diseases: Early Blight, Late Blight, Black Scurf
disease_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, cool nights with heavy morning dew, and water standing in the field
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any extra water and remove weeds to let sunlight reach the soil. Natural control: Spray liquid waste from cows or friendly bio-fungicides like Trichoderma on the soil. Spray if needed: Spray a copper-based medicine on the leaves immediately if you see dark brown spots.

susceptible_pests: Aphids, whiteflies, potato tuber moth, leafhoppers
pest_risk_factors: Warm and dry weather, cracked soil that lets moths reach the underground potatoes, and weeds around the field
pest_management: Field care: Keep the soil well-covered around the plant base to close any cracks so moths cannot lay eggs on the potatoes. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water early in the morning. Spray if needed: Use a mild pest medicine recommended by your local cooperative if you see too many sticky leaves.
susceptible_diseases: Late blight, early blight, black scurf
disease_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, cool nights with heavy dew, wet soil, and water standing in the field for too long
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any extra water from the field and remove infected yellow leaves. Natural control: Spray the crop with liquid made from cow dung and neem leaves. Spray if needed: Spray a copper-based medicine on a clear, sunny day to stop the rot from spreading.

susceptible_pests: Potato tuber moth, Aphids, Whiteflies
pest_risk_factors: Dry soil, cracked soil, warm weather, and leaving harvested potatoes exposed in the open sun.
pest_management: Field care: Keep the soil well-covered around the plants so tubers are not exposed to the sun, and fill any cracks in the soil. Natural control: Use light traps at night to catch moths and spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: If the pest attack is very high, spray a mild insect medicine recommended by your local cooperative shop during the evening.
susceptible_diseases: Late blight, Early blight, Tuber rot
disease_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, cool nights with heavy dew, wet soil, and water standing in the field.
disease_management: Field care: Stop watering the crop 10 to 14 days before digging them out, and cut the top green leafy parts if blight is seen. Natural control: Spray the crop with liquid cow dung extract or sour buttermilk mixed in water to prevent rot. Spray if needed: Spray a basic blue copper medicine on the leaves if you see dark spots spreading fast.

susceptible_pests: shoot gall maker, bark eating caterpillar, aphids
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, neglected orchards with dead wood and unpruned branches
pest_management: Field care: Clean the tree trunks and remove any webs or wooden dust. Poke a thin wire inside the bark holes to kill caterpillars. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the branches. Spray if needed: Use a mild insect spray or inject a few drops of kerosene into the bark holes and seal them with wet mud.
susceptible_diseases: rust, fruit rot, powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: heavy morning dew, damp weather, water pooling around the tree base, and fallen infected leaves
disease_management: Field care: Keep the ground under the tree clean by removing fallen leaves and rotten fruits. Avoid watering the tree trunk directly. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper or sulphur powder mixed in water to protect the growing berries.

susceptible_pests: aphids, seed wasps, brown mites
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, late-season warmth, dry soil, and keeping the harvested crop in the open field for too long
pest_management: Field care: Harvest the crop early in the morning when the dew is still on the plants to prevent seed shattering and pest movement. Natural control: Shake the plants gently over a cloth to collect and destroy pests, and dry the seeds on clean plastic sheets. Spray if needed: Since this is the final harvest stage, avoid chemical sprays entirely to prevent poison in the seeds; use a mild neem water spray only if pests are seen on the drying seeds.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, grain mold, stem gall
disease_risk_factors: high humidity, sudden unseasonal rains, dew on the mature seeds, and piling wet plants together
disease_management: Field care: Cut the plants when the seeds turn from green to a light brown color, and do not pile wet plants in heaps. Natural control: Dry the harvested plants in a clean, shaded, and well-ventilated area rather than direct harsh sunlight to keep the seeds bright and disease-free. Spray if needed: Do not use any chemical sprays at this stage; ensure the seeds are dried until they have no moisture left before storing them in clean, dry gunny bags.

susceptible_pests: cutworms, hairy caterpillars, grasshoppers
pest_risk_factors: dry soil with weeds, fields not ploughed well before sowing, cloudy days
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and remove all weeds around the young sprouts. Hand-pick and destroy any caterpillars you see in the morning. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water on the tiny plants. Spray if needed: If pest damage is high, spray a mild, commonly available insect medicine from the local store during the evening.
susceptible_diseases: seedling blight, root rot, damping-off
disease_risk_factors: heavy rains, water standing in the field, clayey soil that stays wet, sowing seeds too deep
disease_management: Field care: Make small channels to drain out excess rainwater quickly so soil does not stay soggy. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungus powder like Trichoderma in well-rotted cow dung and apply it near the plant roots. Spray if needed: If young plants start rotting and falling over, drench the soil around them with a basic copper-based medicine mixed in water.

sub_stage_name: Early Vegetative Growth and Leaf Development
susceptible_pests: semilooper caterpillar, hairy caterpillar, leafhopper, thrips
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, and weeds growing around the crop
pest_management: Field care: Handpick and destroy any visible caterpillars and their eggs from the leaves. Keep the field free of weeds. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: If the pest attack is severe, spray a mild, commonly available insect medicine from the local store during the evening.
susceptible_diseases: seedling blight, root rot, leaf spot
disease_risk_factors: water pooling in the field, heavy clay soil, and continuous rainy days
disease_management: Field care: Make small channels to drain out excess rainwater quickly so water does not stand near the roots. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma into the soil around the plants. Spray if needed: If spots appear on leaves, spray a basic copper-based medicine mixed in water on a clear, sunny day.

susceptible_pests: Semilooper caterpillar, hairy caterpillar, leafhopper, thrips
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, and dense green leaves that attract egg-laying moths
pest_management: Field care: Walk through the field daily and hand-pick any large caterpillars or leaf-folding webs you see. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: If the leaf damage is very high, spray a mild insect-killing medicine recommended by your local cooperative shop during the cool evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: Seedling blight, leaf spot, root rot
disease_risk_factors: Water pooling in the field, heavy rains, and poor drainage around the plant roots
disease_management: Field care: Dig small channels to drain out any standing water from the field immediately. Natural control: Mix friendly soil fungus powder like Trichoderma with well-rotted cow dung and apply it near the plant roots. Spray if needed: If dark spots spread fast on the leaves, spray a basic copper-based medicine mixed in water to protect the new branches.

susceptible_pests: fruit borer caterpillar, bark eating caterpillar, mealybugs
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, dense branches blocking sunlight, and leaving fallen fruits on the ground
pest_management: Field care: Collect and bury all fallen and damaged fruits deep in the soil to kill hidden worms. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky cards on branches and spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the fruits. Spray if needed: If the attack is severe, spray a mild insect medicine recommended by your local cooperative during the early morning hours.
susceptible_diseases: fruit rot, dry rust, blue mold
disease_risk_factors: high humidity, winter dew, and injuries on the fruit skin during picking
disease_management: Field care: Clip off dry and diseased twigs before picking, and handle fruits gently to avoid scratches. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the trees to prevent rot. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine on the trees after harvest to keep the branches clean and healthy.

susceptible_pests: Semilooper caterpillar, hairy caterpillar, capsule borer, thrips
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, and dense green leaves on the plant
pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy big caterpillars and their eggs from the leaves. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe insect spray from the local store only on the affected flowering branches during the evening.
susceptible_diseases: Wilt, leaf spot, seedling blight
disease_risk_factors: Water standing in the field, heavy rains, and continuous damp weather
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any standing water from the field immediately and pull out dead plants. Natural control: Mix friendly Trichoderma powder in well-rotted cow dung and apply it near the plant roots. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based blue medicine on the leaves if spots start to spread.

susceptible_pests: Castor semilooper, capsule borer, tobacco caterpillar, thrips
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, and dense green leaves at the time of capsule formation
pest_management: Field care: Handpick and destroy large hairy caterpillars and semiloopers from the pods. Natural control: Set up bird perches in the field so birds can eat the caterpillars, and spray neem seed kernel extract. Spray if needed: If capsule damage is high, spray a mild insecticide like spinosad or chlorantraniliprole mixed in water during the evening.
susceptible_diseases: Botrytis gray mold, seedling blight, wilt
disease_risk_factors: Continuous rains, heavy morning dew, and waterlogging around the plant roots
disease_management: Field care: Remove and burn infected capsule bunches showing gray mold immediately to stop the spread. Natural control: Spray the crop with Trichoderma bio-fungicide mixed in water. Spray if needed: If the mold continues to spread during rains, spray carbendazim or mancozeb on the flower and capsule clusters.

sub_stage_name: Maturity and Drying of Primary Spikes
susceptible_pests: semilooper caterpillar, capsule borer, hairy caterpillar
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, and leaving dried leaves on the ground
pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy any large caterpillars found on the spikes. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the plants. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe insect spray recommended by your local cooperative only if the damage is very high.
susceptible_diseases: capsule rot, wilt, seedling blight
disease_risk_factors: sudden winter rains, heavy morning dew, and water logging in the field
disease_management: Field care: Cut and burn infected spikes immediately to stop the spread. Natural control: Apply trichoderma bio-powder mixed with farm manure near the plant roots. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine on the healthy spikes if you see rot spreading during cloudy days.

susceptible_pests: castor semilooper, capsule borer, hairy caterpillar
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, and leaving dry or damaged capsules on the plant for too long
pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy any large caterpillars and bored capsules during your first harvest. Natural control: Set up wooden bird perches in the field to let birds eat the caterpillars, and use neem seed kernel spray. Spray if needed: If the pest attack is very high, spray a mild, safe insecticide on the remaining green capsules.
susceptible_diseases: capsule rot, wilt, seedling blight
disease_risk_factors: unseasonal winter rains, heavy morning dew, and water logging in the field
disease_management: Field care: Harvest only the mature, dry spikes and keep them in a clean, dry place. Natural control: Remove and burn any rotten or black-spotted capsules immediately to stop the spread. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine on the healthy spikes if you see rot spreading due to sudden rains.

susceptible_pests: Semilooper caterpillar, Capsule borer, Tobacco caterpillar
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, warm days, and leaving dried or damaged spikes on the plant
pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy big caterpillars from the spikes during picking. Natural control: Spray neem seed kernel extract or neem oil on the green spikes to stop feeding. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe insect spray only on the green spikes if you see heavy caterpillar damage.
susceptible_diseases: Botrytis gray mold, Seedling blight, Wilt
disease_risk_factors: Unseasonal winter rains, heavy morning dew, and high humidity in the crop canopy
disease_management: Field care: Cut and burn infected spikes immediately to stop the rot from spreading to healthy spikes. Natural control: Spray a mixture of friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma mixed in water on the spikes. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine on the remaining green spikes if the gray mold spreads due to wet weather.

susceptible_pests: Spider mites, whiteflies, aphids, mealybugs
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, dusty roads near the field, and weeds growing around the papaya plants.
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field free of weeds and gently wash the plants with a water spray to remove dust. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water on the underside of the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild soap spray or consult the local shop for a safe medicine to control sucking pests if the attack is very high.
susceptible_diseases: Fruit rot, powdery mildew, papaya ring spot virus
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, cloudy days, water standing near the roots, and pests like aphids carrying the virus from sick plants.
disease_management: Field care: Remove any infected or yellowing leaves and bury them far away from the field. Natural control: Ensure water drains out quickly and does not touch the tree trunk. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine on the fruits and trunk to prevent rotting during rainy days.

susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, cutworms, ants
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, warm sunny days, and crop debris left in the field from the previous harvest
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and hand-pick any bright red beetles seen on the tiny leaves. Natural control: Sprinkle wood ash on the young seedlings early in the morning when they are wet with dew to keep beetles away. Spray if needed: Mix five milliliters of neem oil in one liter of water with a few drops of liquid soap and spray it gently on the seedlings.
susceptible_diseases: seedling rot, damping-off
disease_risk_factors: too much water in the soil, clayey soil that does not drain, and sowing seeds too deep in wet mud
disease_management: Field care: Do not let water stand in the nursery beds and always sow seeds on raised beds to drain extra water. Natural control: Mix friendly fungus powder like Trichoderma into the compost before sowing to protect the seeds. Spray if needed: If seedlings start falling over, drench the soil around them with a simple copper-based blue medicine mixed in water.

susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, aphids, leaf miners
pest_risk_factors: warm sunny days, dry soil, and weeds growing around the young plants

Natural control: Avoid harvesting during wet morning hours to prevent rot. Spray if needed: If wet weather persists and pods start turning black, spray a basic copper-based medicine mixed in water.

pest_risk_factors: dry weather during harvest, late harvesting, weeds left in the field
pest_management: Field care: Harvest the crop as soon as pods turn golden brown to avoid pest attacks on dry pods. Clear out all weeds around the field. susceptible_diseases: pod blight, charcoal rot, pod rot
disease_risk_factors: sudden late rains, high moisture in the soil, keeping harvested plants in wet piles
disease_management: Field care: Harvest on dry days and do not let harvested plants touch wet soil. Dry the harvested pods well in the sun before threshing.
