susceptible_pests: Thrips, Aphids, Whiteflies, Mites
pest_risk_factors: Dry weather with high heat, cloudy skies, and too many weeds around the field.
pest_management: Field care: Remove all weeds from the field borders and hang yellow and blue sticky cards to catch flying insects. Natural control: Spray neem water on the leaves early in the morning to keep pests away. Spray if needed: If leaves start curling, use a mild insect-killing spray from your local cooperative store.
susceptible_diseases: Root rot, Collar rot, Damping-off
disease_risk_factors: Standing water in the field, heavy clay soil, and planting the seedlings too deep in wet soil.
disease_management: Field care: Make small channels to drain out extra water and keep the soil loose around the roots. Natural control: Apply friendly fungus powder mixed with rotten cow dung near the plant roots to fight bad soil germs. Spray if needed: Drench the soil around the plant base with a copper-based blue medicine to stop the roots from rotting.

susceptible_pests: Rice bug, Gundhi bug, Earhead bug
pest_risk_factors: High humidity, cloudy weather, late planting, presence of weeds
pest_management: Cultural: Weed management, avoid late planting. Biological: Conserve natural enemies. Chemical: Foliar spray of Chlorpyrifos, Fipronil.
susceptible_diseases: False smut, Grain discoloration, Brown spot
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, rainfall during grain filling, late planting, poor drainage
disease_management: Cultural: Proper drainage, avoid late planting. Biological: Apply Bacillus subtilis. Chemical: Foliar spray of Propiconazole, Copper oxychloride, Mancozeb.

susceptible_pests: Termites, Shoot borer
pest_risk_factors: Dry soil, waterlogging, high humidity, poor soil preparation, use of untreated seed
pest_management: Cultural: Use healthy seed material, proper soil preparation, avoid waterlogging. Biological: Application of entomopathogenic fungi like Metarhizium anisopliae. Chemical: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid, soil application of Chlorpyrifos.
susceptible_diseases: Red rot, Smut
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, waterlogging, use of infected seed, continuous cropping of sugarcane
disease_management: Cultural: Use disease-free seed, crop rotation, proper drainage. Biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride. Chemical: Seed treatment with Carbendazim, dipping settlings in fungicide solution.

susceptible_pests: Early shoot borer, Stalk borer, Pyrilla
pest_risk_factors: High humidity, warm temperatures, nitrogen-rich fertilization, monoculture
pest_management: Cultural: Remove affected tillers, avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Biological: Release of parasitoids like Trichogramma chilonis, use of biopesticides based on Bacillus thuringiensis. Chemical: Application of Chlorpyrifos, Fipronil, Dimethoate.
susceptible_diseases: Red rot, Wilt
disease_risk_factors: Waterlogged conditions, soil salinity, nutrient deficiency, continuous sugarcane cropping
disease_management: Cultural: Crop rotation, proper drainage, use of resistant varieties. Biological: Soil application of Trichoderma harzianum. Chemical: Soil drenching with Carbendazim, application of Propiconazole.

susceptible_pests: Rats, Termites (on stubble)
pest_risk_factors: Poor field sanitation, availability of alternative food sources, unharvested cane
pest_management: Cultural: Proper field sanitation, removal of stubble, rat control measures. Biological: Use of rodenticides with caution. Chemical: Application of insecticides to control termites in stubble.
susceptible_diseases: Stubble rot
disease_risk_factors: Poor drainage, infected stubble, continuous cropping, lack of sanitation
disease_management: Cultural: Removal and burning of infected stubble, crop rotation, proper drainage. Biological: Soil application of Trichoderma viride. Chemical: Application of fungicides to the soil after harvest.

susceptible_pests: shoot borer, root grubs, thrips
pest_risk_factors: too much shade, damp soil, dry weather spells, and weeds around the young sprouts
pest_management: Field care: Keep the nursery beds clean and remove all weeds gently by hand. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the tiny leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe insect spray from the local shop if you see holes in the leaves.
susceptible_diseases: clump rot, damping-off, leaf spot
disease_risk_factors: water pooling in the beds, heavy clay soil, too much shade, and crowded sowing
disease_management: Field care: Make sure extra water drains out of the beds quickly and reduce the overhead shade slightly to let in light. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma into the soil before and after sprouting. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based blue medicine on the soil and baby plants to stop rotting.

susceptible_pests: fruit fly, tea mosquito bug, mealybug, aphids
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, water pooling near tree trunks, and dense branches that block sunlight
pest_management: Field care: Hang yellow sticky traps and homemade basil leaf traps to catch fruit flies. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the undersides of leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe insect spray only in the evening to protect honeybees that help in pollination.
susceptible_diseases: anthracnose, fruit rot, wilt
disease_risk_factors: continuous rains, waterlogging in the orchard, and damaged or dead branches left on the tree
disease_management: Field care: Keep the basin around the tree clean and drain out any standing water immediately. Natural control: Apply a paste of cow dung and turmeric on pruned branch ends. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine on the flowers and small fruits to stop rotting.

susceptible_pests: fruit fly, tea mosquito bug, mealybug, aphids
pest_risk_factors: warm weather with high humidity, cloudy days, and weeds growing under the tree canopy
pest_management: Field care: Hang simple plastic bottles with basil leaf paste or wooden blocks soaked in sweet water to trap fruit flies. Keep the ground clean and remove any fallen tiny fruits. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the branches. Spray if needed: Use a mild insect-killing spray recommended by your local cooperative if you see sticky webs or tiny bugs on the small fruits.
susceptible_diseases: fruit rot, anthracnose, wilt
disease_risk_factors: heavy rains, water standing around the tree trunk, and crowded branches that do not get sunlight
disease_management: Field care: Cut away dry or dead twigs so sunlight and fresh air can reach inside the tree. Drain out any extra water from the root area. Natural control: Spray a mixture of cow dung and neem leaf extract on the trunk and branches. Spray if needed: Spray a copper-based blue powder medicine mixed in water to protect the young green fruits from rotting.

susceptible_pests: eggplant fruit and shoot borer, red spider mites, whiteflies, jassids
pest_risk_factors: warm and humid weather, cloudy days, dry soil conditions, and leaving damaged fruits rotting on the ground
pest_management: Field care: Walk through your field daily, pluck any wilted shoots or bored fruits, and bury them deep in the soil. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky cards to trap whiteflies and use pheromone traps to catch the borer moths. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water thoroughly on the underside of the leaves every ten days.
susceptible_diseases: fruit rot, phomopsis blight, little leaf disease, collar rot
disease_risk_factors: water pooling around the plants, high humidity, dense leaves blocking sunlight, and not removing old infected plants
disease_management: Field care: Keep the soil around the plant base clean, pluck infected yellow leaves, and ensure water drains out quickly. Natural control: Apply friendly bio-fungicide powder mixed with well-rotted cow dung near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based medicine on a clear sunny day to stop the rot from spreading to healthy fruits.

susceptible_pests: fruit fly, tea mosquito bug, mealybug, bark eating caterpillar
pest_risk_factors: warm and humid weather, cloudy days, water pooling under the trees, and fallen fruits left rotting on the ground
pest_management: Field care: Clean the orchard daily and bury any fallen fruits deep in the soil. Hang simple plastic bottles with basil leaf paste or sweet water to trap fruit flies. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the fruits and branches. Spray if needed: Use a mild insect spray recommended by your local cooperative only on affected branches during the evening.
susceptible_diseases: guava wilt, anthracnose fruit rot, fruit canker
disease_risk_factors: heavy rains, waterlogging around the tree trunk, high humidity, and damage to fruits by birds or insects
disease_management: Field care: Keep the tree basin clean and ensure extra rainwater drains out quickly without touching the trunk. Prune dry or diseased twigs and apply a thick paste of cow dung and turmeric on the cut ends. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungus powder like Trichoderma in well-rotted cow dung manure and apply it near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based blue medicine on the fruits and leaves to stop rotting.

main_stage: Flowering and Shooting Stage : The pseudostem reaches maturity, and the inflorescence  emerges, signaling the start of the reproductive phase
susceptible_pests: banana aphid, stem weevil, thrips, fruit scarring beetle
pest_risk_factors: dry weather with high heat, weeds around the tree base, and leaving old dry leaves hanging on the trunk
pest_management: Field care: Clean the banana trunk by removing old dry leaf sheaths and keep the field free of weeds. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the bunch and trunk. Spray if needed: Use a mild insecticide recommended by your local cooperative shop directly on the fruit bunch and trunk.
susceptible_diseases: sigatoka leaf spot, panama wilt, bunchy top, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: high humidity, water pooling around the roots, cloudy days, and planting too close together
disease_management: Field care: Cut and burn infected leaves, and ensure extra water drains out of the field quickly. Natural control: Apply friendly bio-fungicide powder mixed with cow dung near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine on the leaves and the fruit bunch to stop rotting.

susceptible_pests: Semilooper caterpillar, hairy caterpillar, capsule borer, thrips
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, and dense shade in the field
pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy big caterpillars and their eggs from the leaves. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil. Spray if needed: Use a mild insecticide recommended by your local cooperative if you see more than two caterpillars per plant.
susceptible_diseases: Wilt, seedling blight, leaf spot
disease_risk_factors: Waterlogging in the root zone, heavy rains, and poor drainage in the soil
disease_management: Field care: Remove and burn infected plants immediately and keep the field free of stagnant water. Natural control: Apply Trichoderma powder mixed with well-rotted cow dung near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine on the leaves if spots start spreading rapidly.

sub_stage_name: Seed Germination and Young Seedling Growth
susceptible_pests: Thrips, Aphids, Whiteflies
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, weeds growing near the nursery bed, and keeping the nursery uncovered.
pest_management: Field care: Cover the nursery bed with a thin white net to block insects. Keep the surrounding area free of weeds. Natural control: Spray neem water on the young leaves every week. Spray if needed: If you see tiny insects under the leaves, spray a mild insect medicine from the local store. Always keep the nursery covered with a net to protect young plants.
susceptible_diseases: Damping-off (seedling rot), Collar rot
disease_risk_factors: Too much watering, water standing in the bed, sowing seeds too close to each other, and cloudy weather.
disease_management: Field care: Always grow seedlings on raised beds so extra water drains out easily. Water only in the morning and do not let the soil stay soggy. Natural control: Mix friendly fungus powder like Trichoderma in the soil before sowing. Spray if needed: If young plants start rotting and falling over, spray blue copper medicine mixed in water on the soil. Keep the nursery bed well-drained to save the seedlings.

susceptible_pests: Thrips, yellow mites, aphids, whiteflies, flower caterpillars
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, cloudy days, high humidity, and putting too much urea fertilizer in the soil
pest_management: Field care: Hang yellow sticky cards for whiteflies and blue sticky cards for thrips at the height of the plants. Keep the field free of weeds and do not over-water. Natural control: Spray neem water mixed with a little washing soap on the underside of the leaves where pests hide. Spray if needed: If leaf curling is severe, spray a mild pest medicine recommended by your local cooperative during the cool evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: Twig blight, powdery mildew, root rot, wilt
disease_risk_factors: Water standing in the field, cloudy weather with heavy morning dew, and planting crops too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Clean the drainage channels so water never stands near the roots, and pluck off any drying or blackened twigs immediately. Avoid watering the crop late in the evening. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water on the leaves to prevent white powder disease. Spray if needed: If the tips of the branches start drying downwards, spray a copper-based blue medicine mixed in water to protect the new buds.

sub_stage_name: Fruit Setting and Green Chili Development
susceptible_pests: Thrips, Mites, Fruit borer caterpillar, Aphids
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, cloudy days, using too much urea, and weeds growing around the crop
pest_management: Field care: Hang yellow and blue sticky cards near the plants to catch flying pests, and handpick any chilies with holes. Natural control: Spray neem water or a homemade garlic-chili extract on the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild insect-killing medicine from your local cooperative store if leaf curling becomes severe.
susceptible_diseases: Fruit rot, Powdery mildew, Wet rot
disease_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, water standing in the field, and morning dew on the leaves
disease_management: Field care: Pluck and destroy any rotten chilies immediately, and make sure extra water drains out of the field quickly. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water to protect the leaves. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based medicine or sulfur powder mixed in water to stop the rot from spreading to healthy chilies.

susceptible_pests: Thrips (leaf curl thrips), Pod borer (fruit caterpillar), Mites
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, cloudy days, and using too much urea fertilizer
pest_management: Field care: Hang yellow and blue sticky cards to trap flying pests, and collect and bury any pods with holes. Natural control: Spray neem water on the crop every ten days. Spray if needed: If caterpillar damage is high, spray a safe insect medicine from your local cooperative store.
susceptible_diseases: Fruit rot (anthracnose), Powdery mildew (white ash on leaves)
disease_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, water standing in the field, and crowded plants
disease_management: Field care: Remove any rotten green pods from the plants and clear the weeds to let sunlight in. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water to protect the leaves. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based rot-preventing medicine on a clear, sunny day.

susceptible_pests: Fruit borer caterpillar, Thrips, Yellow mites
pest_risk_factors: Dry and warm weather, cloudy nights, and keeping damaged fruits on the plant
pest_management: Field care: Walk through your field daily and pluck any chili pods with holes in them, then bury them deep in the soil. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky cards to catch small flying insects and use neem spray on the leaves. Spray if needed: If you see many caterpillars, spray a safe pest-clearing medicine bought from your local government cooperative store.
susceptible_diseases: Fruit rot, Ripe rot, Powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: High moisture in the air, heavy morning dew, and plants growing too close together
disease_management: Field care: Pluck and burn any red chilies that show dark, sunken spots to stop the rot from spreading. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the plants to boost their strength. Spray if needed: If the rot spreads, spray a simple copper-based medicine on the pods during a sunny afternoon.

sub_stage_name: Drying on Plant and Multiple Pickings
susceptible_pests: Thrips (leaf curl insects), Mites, Fruit borer caterpillars
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, dry soil, and leaving ripe chilies on the plant for too long
pest_management: Field care: Pick ripe chilies on time and do not let them over-ripen on the plant. Natural control: Hang yellow and blue sticky cards in the field to catch flying insects, and spray neem water. Spray if needed: If insect attack is high, spray a mild soap water solution or consult the local cooperative for a safe pest medicine.
susceptible_diseases: Fruit rot (Anthracnose), Powdery mildew (white ash on leaves)
disease_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, sudden winter rains, heavy morning dew, and keeping infected chilies on the plant
disease_management: Field care: Pluck and burn all rotten or spotted chilies immediately so the disease does not spread to healthy ones. Natural control: Spray a mix of sour buttermilk and water on the plants. Spray if needed: Spray blue copper medicine or sulfur powder mixed in water to save the remaining crop.

susceptible_pests: cutworms, fall armyworm, termites, wireworms
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, weeds in the field, previous crop waste left on the ground, and warm sunny days
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field completely free of weeds and break any hard soil crusts. Natural control: Apply neem cake to the soil and use neem oil spray on young leaves. Spray if needed: If you see cut stems or leaf damage, spray a mild insect medicine around the base of the plants late in the evening.
susceptible_diseases: seed rot, seedling blight, damping-off
disease_risk_factors: water pooling in the field, heavy clay soil, cold wet soil, and planting seeds too deep
disease_management: Field care: Make proper channels to drain out extra rainwater quickly and do not let water stand. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma into the soil or compost before sowing. Spray if needed: If young plants start rotting at the base and falling over, drench the soil around them with a basic copper-based medicine.

susceptible_pests: Fall armyworm, stem borer, corn aphid, cob worm
pest_risk_factors: Warm and dry weather, late sowing, too much nitrogen fertilizer, and weeds around the field boundaries
pest_management: Field care: Handpick and destroy any visible caterpillars and egg masses from the tassels and silks. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water directly into the whorls and on the developing cobs. Spray if needed: If the attack is severe, spray a mild, recommended insect poison using a backpack sprayer directly on the cobs and tassels during the evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: Turcicum leaf blight, Maydis leaf blight, banded leaf and sheath blight, tassel smut
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, cloudy days, water pooling in the field, and plants sown too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any standing water from the field and remove the infected lower leaves to let air and sunlight pass through. Natural control: Spray a mixture of cow urine and water, or use bio-powders like Trichoderma mixed with well-rotted cow dung near the roots. Spray if needed: If dark spots spread rapidly on the leaves, spray a basic copper-based medicine or a standard disease-control powder mixed in water.

susceptible_pests: fall armyworm, stem borer, cob worm, aphids
pest_risk_factors: warm and dry weather, late sowing, weeds around the field, and lack of bird perches
pest_management: Field care: Handpick and destroy any caterpillars found inside the cob covers. Natural control: Release friendly predator wasps and place wooden bird perches to attract birds that eat worms. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water directly on the cobs and silk if you see heavy pest damage.
susceptible_diseases: leaf blight, rust, cob rot
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, water standing in the field, and crowded plants
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any excess water from the field and remove infected lower leaves to let in sunlight. Natural control: Spray liquid fermented cow dung manure mixed with water to boost plant strength. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine on the leaves if dark spots spread rapidly.

susceptible_pests: leaf miner, aphids, thrips, red hairy caterpillar
pest_risk_factors: dry weather with no rain, hot sunny days, and weeds growing around the crop
pest_management: Field care: Pull out weeds regularly and set up yellow sticky traps to catch flying insects. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: If the leaf damage is high, spray a mild insect medicine recommended by your local cooperative store during the cool evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: collar rot, stem rot, early leaf spot
disease_risk_factors: too much water in the soil, cloudy weather, and sowing seeds too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any standing water from the field and remove weak, dying plants. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungicide powder like Trichoderma into the soil around the plants. Spray if needed: If you see dark spots on leaves or rotting at the base, spray a basic copper-based medicine on the plants to stop it from spreading.

susceptible_pests: leaf miner, red hairy caterpillar, tobacco caterpillar, aphids
pest_risk_factors: dry weather with no rain, cloudy days, and weeds left growing around the field
pest_management: Field care: Handpick and destroy visible caterpillars and their eggs from the leaves. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: Use a mild, government-approved insect spray recommended by your local cooperative during the evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: tikka leaf spot, collar rot, stem rot
disease_risk_factors: high humidity, continuous wet soil, warm weather, and plants crowded too close together
disease_management: Field care: Remove any yellowing or rotting plants immediately and keep the soil loose around the base. Natural control: Apply trichoderma powder mixed with well-rotted cow dung near the plant roots. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper-based medicine or a simple fungicide recommended by your local agricultural officer if dark spots spread rapidly.

susceptible_pests: leaf miner, red hairy caterpillar, tobacco caterpillar, white grub
pest_risk_factors: dry weather with no rain, sandy soils, weeds around the field, and cloudy nights
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field free of weeds and set up simple light traps at night to catch adult moths. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: If the leaf damage is high, spray a mild, recommended pest medicine from your local cooperative store during the late afternoon.
susceptible_diseases: early leaf spot, late leaf spot, rust, collar rot
disease_risk_factors: continuous wet weather, high humidity, water standing in the field, and crowded plants
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any extra water from the field and remove infected yellow leaves. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water, or use Trichoderma powder mixed with organic manure near the roots. Spray if needed: If dark spots spread rapidly on the leaves, spray a basic copper-based medicine or a standard disease-control powder recommended by your local agriculture officer.

susceptible_pests: pod borer, red hairy caterpillar, white grub, termites
pest_risk_factors: dry soil during maturity, late harvesting, cracked soil, and leaving crop residue in the field
pest_management: Field care: Harvest the crop on time without delay to prevent termites from damaging the pods. Dig out and destroy white grubs if seen in the soil. Natural control: Apply neem cake to the soil and use light traps at night to catch adult moths. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with soap water on the leaves if you see caterpillars eating the foliage.
susceptible_diseases: tikka leaf spot, rust, collar rot, pod rot
disease_risk_factors: high humidity, wet soil from late rains, waterlogging in the field, and cloudy weather
disease_management: Field care: Drain out any excess water from the field and remove infected plants immediately. Natural control: Spray the crop with a mixture of sour buttermilk and water to check fungal growth. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based medicine or simple sulfur powder mixed in water if the leaf spots cover more than half the field.

susceptible_pests: ants, termites, leaf-cutting weevils
pest_risk_factors: dry soil, rotting organic matter near the seeds, and piles of dry leaves around the nursery bed
pest_management: Field care: Keep the nursery area clean and remove any dry leaves or rotting wood. Natural control: Pour neem water around the germinating seeds to keep ants and termites away. Spray if needed: Spray a mild neem oil mixture on the tiny new leaves if you see insects biting them.
susceptible_diseases: seedling rot, damping-off, seed mold
disease_risk_factors: too much watering, water standing in the soil, and keeping the nursery bed in deep shade with no sunlight
disease_management: Field care: Water the soil gently without making it muddy, and ensure extra water drains away quickly. Natural control: Mix wood ash in the soil before sowing and let the nursery get mild morning sunlight. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based blue medicine water on the soil if the baby plants start rotting at the base.

main_stage: Flowering to Fruit Set: Occurs in late winter/early spring
susceptible_pests: Mango hopper, mealybug, fruit fly
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, high humidity, crowded tree branches, and warm sunny days during fruit ripening
pest_management: Field care: Keep the orchard clean, remove fallen fruits, and tie sticky plastic bands around the tree trunk to stop crawling bugs. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the trunk and branches, and hang yellow sticky traps. Spray if needed: Use a mild insecticide spray recommended by your local cooperative if the hopper attack is very high.
susceptible_diseases: Powdery mildew, anthracnose black spots, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: Sudden unseasonal rains, heavy morning dew, cloudy skies, and poor air flow inside the tree canopy
disease_management: Field care: Prune dead and dry twigs to let sunlight reach inside the tree, and collect and burn infected fallen leaves. Natural control: Spray diluted sour buttermilk or bio-fungicides like Trichoderma on the leaves. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper or sulphur powder mixed in water during dry hours if black spots start spreading on the young fruits.

susceptible_pests: mustard aphid, painted bug
pest_risk_factors: dry weather, late harvesting, piles of harvested crop left in the field for too long
pest_management: Field care: Harvest the crop on time without delay and clean the field boundaries. Natural control: Keep the harvested bundles in bright sunlight to drive away the bugs. Spray if needed: No chemical spray is recommended at this final stage to avoid chemical residue in the mustard oil.
susceptible_diseases: white rust, alternaria blight, powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high moisture in the air, keeping harvested plants in damp shady areas
disease_management: Field care: Cut the crop when leaves turn yellow and pods turn golden brown. Natural control: Dry the harvested crop under direct, bright sunlight on a clean floor. Spray if needed: Do not spray any chemicals now as the crop is ready for threshing.

susceptible_pests: Termites, Cutworms
pest_risk_factors: Dry soil, using raw or un-rotted cow dung manure, and leaving old crop waste in the field.
pest_management: Field care: Remove all old crop roots and use only fully rotted cow dung manure. Natural control: Mix neem cake into the soil during land preparation to keep pests away. Spray if needed: If you see cutworms cutting the small plants, spray neem water on the soil around the seedlings in the evening. Always keep the soil moist but not wet to prevent termites.
susceptible_diseases: Seedling rot, Damping-off
disease_risk_factors: Water standing in the field, sowing seeds too deep, and very wet and cold soil.
disease_management: Field care: Make small channels to drain out extra rainwater or irrigation water quickly. Natural control: Mix friendly bio-fungus powder like Trichoderma in the soil before sowing to protect young roots. Spray if needed: If young plants start falling over and rotting at the ground level, spray a simple copper medicine on the soil around the plants. Keep the soil loose so air can reach the roots.

susceptible_pests: Aphids (Lahi), Armyworms, Stem borers
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, warm days, and putting too much urea fertilizer in the soil
pest_management: Field care: Walk through your field daily and pull out any heavily infested plants. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky cards near the crop tops and spray neem water on the plants. Spray if needed: If you see more than ten pests on a single stem, use a mild pest control spray from your local cooperative store.
susceptible_diseases: Leaf rust (Gairui), Powdery mildew (white ash on leaves), Loose smut (black powder in grain heads)
disease_risk_factors: Heavy morning dew, cloudy skies, and water standing in the field for too long
disease_management: Field care: Stop watering the field during cloudy days and ensure extra water drains out quickly. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves to stop the spread of white ash. Spray if needed: If you see orange spots or black powder on the grain heads, spray a basic copper medicine immediately to save your yield.

susceptible_pests: Aphids (Lahi or Mahua), Armyworms, Birds
pest_risk_factors: Cloudy weather, warm days, dry winds, and dense plants
pest_management: Field care: Walk through the field daily, install shiny ribbons or scarecrows to keep birds away, and remove weeds. Natural control: Spray homemade neem water on the plants and let friendly ladybug beetles eat the pests. Spray if needed: If the pest attack is very high, spray a mild insect medicine from the local cooperative store.
susceptible_diseases: Leaf Rust (Gerui or Rattua), Powdery Mildew (Safed Churna), Loose Smut (Kala Koyla)
disease_risk_factors: Heavy morning dew, cloudy skies, too much moisture in the soil, and dense sowing
disease_management: Field care: Avoid watering the field in the evening and remove any black-headed grain ears carefully in a plastic bag. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves. Spray if needed: If orange rust spots or white powder covers the leaves, spray a basic copper or sulfur medicine mixed in water.

susceptible_pests: Green leafhoppers (Jassids), Aphids, Whiteflies
pest_risk_factors: Warm and cloudy weather, dry soil, and weeds growing around the crop
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field free of weeds and hang yellow sticky cards to trap flying insects. Natural control: Spray neem water mixed with a little liquid soap on the underside of the leaves. Spray if needed: If the attack is severe, use a safe, basic insect spray from your local government depot.
susceptible_diseases: Yellow vein disease (leaves turning yellow), Root rot
disease_risk_factors: Water standing in the field, high moisture in the air, and whiteflies spreading the yellow virus
disease_management: Field care: Make sure excess water drains out of the field quickly and remove any yellowing plants immediately. Natural control: Mix useful soil fungus like Trichoderma in compost and apply near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper medicine if you see rotting or dark spots on the stems.

susceptible_pests: Green leafhoppers, Aphids, Whiteflies, Shoot borer
pest_risk_factors: Warm and cloudy weather, high humidity, and putting too much urea fertilizer which makes the plants soft and juicy
pest_management: Field care: Cut off and bury any wilting shoots that have borers inside, and hang yellow sticky cards to catch flying pests. Natural control: Spray neem water on the leaves to keep pests away. Spray if needed: If pest numbers are very high, ask your local cooperative for a safe pest-control medicine to spray.
susceptible_diseases: Yellow vein disease, Powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, morning dew, weeds in the field, and whiteflies carrying the yellow virus from plant to plant
disease_management: Field care: Pull out any plants that start turning yellow and bury them far away from the field. Natural control: Spray a mix of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves to stop white powder. Spray if needed: If the white powder spreads, spray a simple sulphur-based medicine mixed in water.

susceptible_pests: scale insects, bark beetles, olive fruit fly
pest_risk_factors: dry winter weather, unpruned dead wood, and piles of fallen leaves left under the trees
pest_management: Field care: Prune and burn all dead and dry branches to remove hiding spots. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the tree trunk and branches. Spray if needed: Use a mild, common insect spray on the bark if you see sticky scale insects.
susceptible_diseases: peacock spot, olive knot, root rot
disease_risk_factors: heavy winter rains, high humidity, water logging around the roots, and open wounds from pruning
disease_management: Field care: Keep the tree basin clean and drain out any standing water. Natural control: Apply a thick paste of cow dung and turmeric on cut branches after pruning. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based blue medicine on the leaves to prevent winter spots.

main_stage: Flowering and Fruit Set : Flowers appear after a period of stress
susceptible_pests: Citrus psylla, fruit sucking moth, citrus leaf miner, spider mites
pest_risk_factors: Warm and dry weather, new soft green leaves, and fallen rotten fruits left on the ground
pest_management: Field care: Keep the orchard clean by burying any fallen fruits in a deep pit. Natural control: Hang yellow sticky cards on branches to catch flying pests and spray neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: Use a mild insect spray recommended by your local cooperative during early morning hours.
susceptible_diseases: Gummosis, fruit rot, citrus canker
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, water standing around the tree trunk, and cloudy weather with light rains
disease_management: Field care: Do not let irrigation water touch the tree trunk directly and make a ring of soil around the base to keep water away. Natural control: Apply a thick paste of cow dung and copper lime mixture on the lower trunk up to two feet high. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper medicine on the leaves and fruits to stop rotting.

susceptible_pests: Cutworms, white grubs, seed maggots, and birds.
pest_risk_factors: Using fresh or unrotted cow dung manure, dry soil conditions, and leaving weeds in the field.
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and scare away birds during morning and evening hours. Natural control: Use only well-rotted cow dung manure and apply neem cake to the soil before sowing. Spray if needed: Spray neem water on the soil around the sprouts if you see insects cutting the young plants.
susceptible_diseases: Seed rot, seedling rot, and collar rot.
disease_risk_factors: Waterlogging in the field, heavy rains right after sowing, and sowing seeds too deep in wet soil.
disease_management: Field care: Make proper channels to drain out excess rainwater quickly so that water does not stand in the field. Natural control: Always treat the seeds with friendly fungus powder like Trichoderma before sowing. Spray if needed: If young plants start rotting and falling over, mix a basic copper medicine in water and pour it near the roots of the plants.

susceptible_pests: Cutworms, Stem fly, Whitefly
pest_risk_factors: Hot and dry weather, weeds in the field, and crop waste left from the last harvest
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and remove all weeds that hide pests. Natural control: Spray neem water on the tiny seedlings to stop flies from laying eggs. Spray if needed: If insects are cutting the baby plants at night, spray a simple insect-killing medicine on the soil around the plants in the evening.
susceptible_diseases: Seedling rot, Collar rot, Root rot
disease_risk_factors: Water standing in the field, sowing seeds too deep, and very wet soil
disease_management: Field care: Make proper channels to drain out extra rainwater so it does not stand near the seedlings. Natural control: Always treat the seeds with friendly bio-powders like Trichoderma before sowing to protect them. Spray if needed: If you see young plants rotting and falling over, spray a basic copper-based medicine near the roots immediately.

susceptible_pests: fruit fly, mealybug, scale insects, birds
pest_risk_factors: warm weather, high humidity, ripe fruits left on the tree, fallen fruits lying on the ground
pest_management: Field care: Harvest fruits when they turn light green to yellow, and do not let them over-ripen on the tree. Collect and deeply bury all fallen and damaged fruits to stop pests from breeding. Natural control: Hang simple plastic bottles with basil leaf paste or fruit fly traps in the orchard to catch male flies. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the branches and fruits to keep mealybugs away.
susceptible_diseases: fruit rot, anthracnose, sooty mould
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, continuous rains, water dripping from leaves, dense branches that block sunlight
disease_management: Field care: Prune lower branches that touch the ground and remove dry twigs to let sunlight and air pass through the tree. Natural control: Spray a mixture of turmeric powder and wood ash on the fruits to prevent rotting. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based blue medicine powder mixed in water on the fruits and leaves to stop the rot from spreading.

susceptible_pests: San Jose scale, apple stem borer, codling moth, woolly aphid
pest_risk_factors: Dry weather, uncleaned orchards, piled-up wooden crates, and dead wood left near the trees
pest_management: Field care: Clean the orchard floor and remove any fallen or damaged fruits immediately. Natural control: Hang cardboard traps on tree trunks to catch crawling pests. Spray if needed: Use a simple neem oil spray on the tree trunks after harvesting is complete.
susceptible_diseases: Apple scab, bitter rot, sooty blotch, flyspeck
disease_risk_factors: High humidity, continuous rains during picking, dense tree branches that block sunlight, and wet grass under the trees
disease_management: Field care: Keep the ground clear of fallen leaves and prune away crowded branches to let in sunlight. Natural control: Spray cow urine mixed with water on the soil to stop disease spores from spreading. Spray if needed: Apply a basic copper-based blue copper spray on the trees right after you finish harvesting the fruits.

susceptible_pests: cutworms, lucerne caterpillars, wireworms
pest_risk_factors: dry soil conditions, presence of weeds in the field, and leftover crop waste from the previous season
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and remove all weeds that hide young pests. Natural control: Use neem oil spray on the young seedlings and place T-shaped wooden bird perches in the field so birds can eat the caterpillars. Spray if needed: If pest damage is high, spray a mild, safe insecticide recommended by your local cooperative during the evening hours.
susceptible_diseases: seedling blight, root rot, wilt
disease_risk_factors: too much water in the soil, heavy clay soils that do not drain well, and cloudy weather with high humidity
disease_management: Field care: Do not let water stand in the field and ensure extra water drains out quickly. Natural control: Apply friendly bio-fungicide powder mixed with well-rotted cow dung near the roots. Spray if needed: If seedlings start rotting, spray a basic copper-based medicine mixed in water directly on the soil around the plants.

susceptible_pests: linseed bud fly, green semilooper caterpillar, aphids
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, and too much nitrogen fertilizer
pest_management: Field care: Handpick and destroy any visible caterpillars and remove weeds around the field. Natural control: Set up bright yellow sticky cards to trap aphids and spray homemade neem seed kernel extract. Spray if needed: If you see many damaged flower buds, spray a mild, clear insecticide recommended by your local cooperative during the evening.
susceptible_diseases: linseed rust, wilt, powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: heavy morning dew, dense planting with no air flow, and wet soil
disease_management: Field care: Pull out and burn any sickly, drying plants immediately to stop the spread. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves to keep mildews away. Spray if needed: If orange rust spots appear on leaves, spray a basic copper-based medicine mixed in water.

susceptible_pests: linseed bud fly, green caterpillars, aphids
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, warm day temperatures, and late sowing
pest_management: Field care: Walk through the field daily and pluck any swollen, damaged flower buds that do not open. Natural control: Set up bright yellow sticky cards to catch flying pests and install T-shaped wooden bird perches to invite birds that eat caterpillars. Spray if needed: Spray neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water thoroughly on the buds.
susceptible_diseases: rust, wilt, powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: heavy morning dew, cool nights with warm days, and crowded plants with no air movement
disease_management: Field care: Pull out and burn any dry, drooping, or yellowing plants immediately. Natural control: Keep the field free of weeds to let sunlight and fresh air reach the base of the plants. Spray if needed: Spray a simple sulfur powder mix or a basic copper spray on the leaves if you see orange spots or white powdery dust.

susceptible_pests: linseed bud fly, green caterpillars, semilooper
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, warm day temperatures, and late sowing
pest_management: Field care: Handpick and destroy any visible caterpillars and damaged buds. Set up bright yellow sticky traps and light traps in the field to catch adult flies. Natural control: Spray homemade neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water. Spray if needed: If the damage is severe, spray a mild, recommended insecticide during the late afternoon when helpful honeybees are not active.
susceptible_diseases: rust, wilt, powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: heavy morning dew, cool nights with warm days, and crowded plants that do not get enough air
disease_management: Field care: Pull out and burn any orange-spotted or dry, withered plants immediately. Keep the field free of weeds to allow sunlight and air to reach the soil. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water, or use bio-powders like Trichoderma mixed in compost. Spray if needed: If orange rust spots or white powdery patches spread, spray a basic sulfur-based powder mixed in water.

sub_stage_name: Drying of Pods and Plant Senescence
susceptible_pests: linseed bud fly, pod borer
pest_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, and late sowing of the crop
pest_management: Field care: Harvest the crop as soon as the pods turn golden brown to avoid pest damage. Natural control: Set up simple bamboo bird perches in the field to invite birds that eat the pod borer worms. Spray if needed: If you see many pests, spray a simple neem seed kernel extract or neem oil mixed with soapy water on the plants.
susceptible_diseases: rust, wilt, powdery mildew
disease_risk_factors: heavy morning dew, cool nights, and damp soil conditions during the drying stage
disease_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and remove any infected dry plants immediately after harvest. Natural control: Avoid watering the crop at this late stage to keep the soil dry and stop fungus growth. Spray if needed: If powdery white spots appear on the leaves, spray a simple sulphur powder mixed in water to protect the remaining crop.

susceptible_pests: Red pumpkin beetle, aphids, leaf miner
pest_risk_factors: Warm sunny days, dry soil, and having old pumpkin or melon fields nearby
pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick the bright red beetles from the young leaves in the early morning when they are slow. Natural control: Sprinkle wood ash on the young leaves to stop the beetles from eating them, or spray neem water. Spray if needed: If the damage is very high, spray a mild insect medicine like dimethoate mixed in water.
susceptible_diseases: Damping-off, powdery mildew, mosaic virus
disease_risk_factors: Too much water in the soil, cloudy weather, and pests like aphids spreading the virus
disease_management: Field care: Do not let water stand near the roots of the small seedlings and remove any weak, yellowing plants immediately. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water on the leaves to prevent white powdery spots. Spray if needed: If the plants start rotting at the base, drench the soil around them with copper oxychloride liquid.

susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, fruit fly, aphids, whiteflies
pest_risk_factors: warm and sunny days, weeds around the vines, wet soil under the leaves
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field free of weeds and gently lift vines off wet soil using dry straw mulch. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with mild soapy water on the leaves early in the morning. Spray if needed: Use a mild, farmer-recommended insect spray only on the affected leaves if the damage is high.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, leaf spot
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, water splashing on leaves, crowded vines
disease_management: Field care: Pluck and bury infected leaves far away from the field, and water only at the base of the plant. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves to stop white powdery spots. Spray if needed: Use a basic copper-based medicine spray during a dry afternoon to protect the new growth.

sub_stage_name: Appearance of Male and Female Flowers
susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, fruit fly, whitefly, aphids
pest_risk_factors: warm sunny days, yellow flowers attracting flies, weeds around the patch, and damp soil under the vines
pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick and destroy the orange-red beetles in the morning. Hang simple plastic bottles with ripe banana mash and a few drops of poison to trap fruit flies. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild, farmer-recommended insect spray only in the late evening so helpful honeybees are not harmed.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, mosaic virus
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, water splashing on leaves, and crowded vines that do not get enough sunlight
disease_management: Field care: Pluck and bury yellow or spotted leaves, and keep the pumpkin fruits off the wet soil using dry straw. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves to stop white powdery spots. Spray if needed: Spray a basic copper or sulfur powder mixed in water if the leaf spots spread rapidly.

susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, fruit fly, whitefly, aphids
pest_risk_factors: warm and humid weather, water pooling near the vines, yellowing leaves, and fallen rotten fruits left in the field
pest_management: Field care: Keep the pumpkin fruits off the wet soil by placing dry straw or wooden boards under them, and bury any damaged fruits deep in the soil. Natural control: Hang simple plastic bottles with ripe banana mash and a few drops of poison to trap fruit flies, and spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: If the beetle attack is very high, spray a mild insect medicine recommended by your local cooperative during the late evening to protect helpful honeybees.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: cloudy days, heavy morning dew, crowded leaves that do not get sunlight, and watering the plants from above
disease_management: Field care: Cut away old, yellow, or crowded leaves near the bottom of the plant to let air and sunlight pass through easily. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk diluted in water or use trichoderma bio-powder mixed in cow dung near the roots. Spray if needed: If you see white powdery spots on the leaves, spray a basic copper or sulphur medicine on a clear, sunny morning.

susceptible_pests: pumpkin beetles, fruit flies, whiteflies
pest_risk_factors: warm and humid weather, rotting fallen fruits left in the field, water touching the growing pumpkins
pest_management: Field care: Place dry straw or wooden plates under growing pumpkins to keep them off the wet soil. Natural control: Hang simple plastic bottles with ripe banana or basil paste to trap fruit flies. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with mild soap water on the leaves and young fruits during early morning hours.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: heavy morning dew, cloudy days, crowded vines that do not get enough sunlight and air
disease_management: Field care: Cut away old, yellowing leaves near the bottom to let air and sunlight reach the fruits. Natural control: Spray a mix of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves to stop white powdery spots. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based medicine or simple baking soda water on the vines if leaves start drying up.

susceptible_pests: Fruit fly, pumpkin beetle, red spider mites
pest_risk_factors: Over-ripe pumpkins left on the ground, damp soil under the fruit, and warm, humid weather
pest_management: Field care: Keep the pumpkins off the wet soil by placing a layer of dry straw or a wooden board underneath them. Natural control: Use simple plastic bottle traps with ripe banana or jaggery to catch fruit flies. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with mild soapy water on the leaves and fruit if you see beetles chewing the skin.
susceptible_diseases: Fruit rot, powdery mildew, downy mildew
disease_risk_factors: Water touching the ripening fruit, heavy morning dew, and watering the plants from above late in the evening
disease_management: Field care: Cut away yellow, dry, or rotting leaves to let sunlight reach the pumpkins and keep the soil dry. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water on the leaves to stop white powdery spots. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based medicine on the soil and fruit if you see soft, watery rot spots starting to form.

main_stage: Transplanting & Establishment: Seedlings are transplanted into the main field during the rainy season . They require 3-4 years to reach maturity
susceptible_pests: coffee berry borer, white stem borer, mealybugs
pest_risk_factors: hot and dry weather before the rains, dense shade trees, and unpicked leftover berries from the previous harvest
pest_management: Field care: Keep the shade balanced to let light in and collect any leftover dry berries from the ground. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the stems and branches. Spray if needed: Use a light spray of soapy water to wash away mealybugs if you see them clustering on the new flower buds.
susceptible_diseases: coffee rust, black rot, damping off
disease_risk_factors: heavy morning mist, high humidity, overcrowded plants, and too much shade
disease_management: Field care: Prune thick branches to let sunlight reach the center of the plant and clear away fallen leaves. Natural control: Spray a mixture of copper-based powder and water on the leaves to protect them. Spray if needed: Apply a mild copper spray on the underside of the leaves before the heavy monsoon rains begin.

main_stage:
Harvesting : The harvesting of cherries in Karnataka usually begins in November and extends to February.
Fly Picking: Early small-scale picking .
Main Picking: Peak harvesting of ripe red cherries, typically in December
susceptible_pests: coffee berry borer, mealybugs, green scale
pest_risk_factors: leaving overripe or fallen berries on the ground, dense shade, and dry warm weather
pest_management: Field care: Collect and destroy all fallen and leftover berries from the ground to stop the borer from breeding. Natural control: Use soapy water spray to wash away mealybugs and scale insects. Spray if needed: Use a light neem oil spray on affected bushes to keep the pests away.
susceptible_diseases: coffee berry rot, black rot, leaf rust
disease_risk_factors: high humidity, wet weather during drying, and keeping harvested cherries in thick, wet heaps for too long
disease_management: Field care: Spread the harvested cherries thinly on clean drying yards and stir them regularly under the sun. Natural control: Keep the drying area clean and free from old, moldy coffee skins. Spray if needed: Spray a simple copper-based mixture on the bushes if you see rotting berries or leaves.

susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, aphids, cutworms
pest_risk_factors: dry soil with hot sunny days, weeds around the young plants, and leaving crop waste from the previous season in the field
pest_management: Field care: Hand-pick the bright orange beetles from the leaves in the early morning when they are slow. Natural control: Sprinkle wood ash on the young leaves to stop beetles from eating them, or spray neem water mixed with a little soap. Spray if needed: If the damage is very high, spray a mild insect medicine recommended by your local cooperative store on a clear afternoon.
susceptible_diseases: damping-off, collar rot
disease_risk_factors: too much water in the soil, cloudy weather, and sowing seeds too close to each other
disease_management: Field care: Avoid overwatering and make sure extra water drains out of the field quickly. Natural control: Mix friendly fungus powder like Trichoderma into the soil around the seedlings to protect the roots. Spray if needed: If seedlings start rotting at the base, drench the soil around them with a basic copper medicine mixed in water.

susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, aphids, whiteflies, leaf miners
pest_risk_factors: warm sunny days, dry soil, weeds around the field, and tender new leaves on the growing vines
pest_management: Field care: Remove weeds regularly and gently loosen the soil around the vines. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves, or sprinkle wood ash on the young leaves early in the morning. Spray if needed: Use a mild insecticide recommended by your local cooperative if the beetle damage is severe.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, damping-off
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, crowded vines, and watering the plants from above
disease_management: Field care: Water only at the base of the plant and avoid wetting the leaves. Natural control: Spray a mixture of sour buttermilk and water, or use a bio-fungicide like Trichoderma in the soil. Spray if needed: Apply a basic copper-based spray if you see yellow or white spots on the leaves.

susceptible_pests: red pumpkin beetle, fruit fly, aphids, whiteflies
pest_risk_factors: warm sunny days, yellow flowers attracting flies, weeds around the field, dry soil
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and remove all weeds. Hang yellow sticky cards to catch small flying pests. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild, safe insect spray on the soil and leaves early in the morning before bees start visiting the flowers.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, water touching the leaves, crowded plants
disease_management: Field care: Water only at the root level and avoid splashing water on the leaves. Remove any yellow or spotted leaves near the ground. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water on the leaves to prevent white powdery spots. Spray if needed: Use a simple copper-based medicine spray on a clear, sunny day.

susceptible_pests: pumpkin beetle, fruit fly, aphids, whitefly
pest_risk_factors: hot and dry days, cloudy weather, water pooling near the plant base, and weeds around the field
pest_management: Field care: Keep the field clean and remove all weeds. Hang yellow sticky cards to catch flying pests. Natural control: Spray neem oil mixed with soapy water on the leaves. Spray if needed: Use a mild, farmer-approved insect spray from the local store only in the late evening so honeybees are not harmed.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: high humidity, heavy morning dew, crowded leaves, and wet soil touching the young fruits
disease_management: Field care: Place dry straw or plastic sheets under the growing melons so they do not touch wet soil. Water only at the roots and avoid wetting the leaves. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water or use trichoderma powder in the soil. Spray if needed: Use a basic copper or sulfur powder spray if white or grey spots appear on the leaves.

susceptible_pests: fruit fly, red pumpkin beetle, aphids, whiteflies
pest_risk_factors: hot and humid weather, water pooling under the fruits, rotting fallen fruits left in the field, weeds around the crop
pest_management: Field care: Keep the melons off the wet soil by placing dry straw or plastic cups under them. Remove and bury any damaged or rotting fruits immediately. Natural control: Hang simple yellow sticky traps and plastic fruit fly traps with bait around the field. Spray if needed: Spray neem oil mixed with mild soap water on the leaves and young fruits.
susceptible_diseases: powdery mildew, downy mildew, fruit rot
disease_risk_factors: cloudy weather, high humidity, watering late in the evening, leaves staying wet for too long
disease_management: Field care: Water only at the soil level and avoid wetting the leaves or fruits. Pluck off old, yellowing leaves from the bottom to let air flow freely. Natural control: Spray sour buttermilk mixed with water, or use trichoderma powder mixed in compost near the roots. Spray if needed: Spray copper-based medicine or simple baking soda water on the leaves at the first sign of white spots.

susceptible_pests: Fruit flies, melon aphids, red pumpkin beetles
pest_risk_factors: Over-ripe fruits left on the ground, hot and humid weather, and weeds around the field
pest_management: Field care: Collect and bury any damaged or fallen fruits immediately to stop flies from breeding. Natural control: Hang simple yellow sticky traps and plastic bottles with sweet basil paste to trap fruit flies.
